title: Vilasa 24. The Life of Advaita Acharya, the Lineages of Mahaprabhu's Associates and the Kulina System of the Bengali Brahmanas
html:
The nature of Krishna, Balarama and Sadashiva; the birth and childhood pastimes of Advaita; his studies, travels, the finding of Madana-gopala and his initiation by Madhavendra Puri; Advaita's disciples and Brahma-Haridasa; Advaita's marriage and family; Madhava Acharya (Kavivallabha); Mahaprabhu's lineage; Vishvarupa and Nityananda; Mahaprabhu's journey to East Bengal; Nityananda's marriage, Virabhadra and Devivara; the family of Gadadhara Pandita; the Radhi and Varendra brahmanas, Adishura, Ballala and the rules of kulinism; the author's conclusion1

1Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaitachandra! Glory to the devotees of Gaura!

2Krishna is Svayam Bhagavan, who sports in Goloka,
dark like a tamala tree, two-armed, holding the flute,

3dark like a fresh raincloud and a bee,
radiant like an indranila gem.

4He is called Brahman, Paramatma, Bhagavan;
sadhakas see His form made of effulgence.

5Within the effulgence they see Sri Shyamasundara —
He is Sri Krishna, Narayana, the Supreme Lord.

6His manifestations (prakasha) are not counted as different [from Him]:
the form manifested by Himself is one, not separate.

7Vasudeva, the root of the fourfold expansion (chatur-vyuha) in Dvaraka,
is a manifestation of Sri Krishna: there is no difference [between them].

8As it is said: "A manifestation is not counted among the different [forms]: it is not separate [from Him]."2

9All know that this Supreme Lord is Krishna;
His vilasa is Narayana, who dwells in Vaikuntha.

10That same Krishna is Narayana, who sports in Vaikuntha,
four-armed, holding conch, disc, club and lotus.

11In self-conception Narayana and Krishna are not different;
vilasa and the other [forms] differ only in appearance.

12Two more vilasas of Krishna are Balarama and Sadashiva:
non-different [from Him], they take the mood of devotees and [appear as] distinct3.

13They only seem distinct because of the devotee's mood;
in truth they are non-different — know this for certain.

14Sankarshana, the root of the chatur-vyuha in Dvaraka,
is the manifested form of Balarama.

15Balarama's vilasa is Maha-Sankarshana in Vaikuntha;
in the chatur-vyuha of Rama he is counted as Lakshmana.

16Sankarshana is one of the four vilasas in the enclosure of Vaikuntha.
Such is the truth of Baladeva; listen further, O hearers.

17Karanodakashayi is the Inner Controller of all the universes,
Garbhodakashayi the Inner Controller of each universe,

18Kshirodakashayi the Inner Controller of each living being,
and Sri Ananta-deva Shesha, who is beyond maya —

19all of them are portions of Balarama.
Who [fully] knows the truth of this Balarama?

20Bed, seat, vehicle, umbrella, sandals —
taking various forms, Balai serves Krishna.

21This Balarama is Nityananda Mahashaya;
he is also Vishvarupa, the brother of Sri Chaitanyadeva.

22For the work of creation Sadashiva, together with Rudra, his own portion,
became manifest from Mahavishnu — know this for certain.

23Therefore Sadashiva is an avatara of Mahavishnu.
O hearers, I have told you the essence.

24There is no difference between Mahavishnu and Sadashiva;
the difference is only for the work of creation — this alone I find.

25Mahavishnu and Sadashiva are one body;
everyone calls it the form of Hari-Hara.

26Mahavishnu-Sadashiva, the benefactor of living beings,
performed austerities for seven hundred years in Kali[-yuga].

27Seeing Krishna face to face, he offered praise and obeisance
and asked the Lord: "How will the living beings of Kali be liberated?"

28Krishna said: "Liberation is in the Name. Listen, Sadashiva:
take birth on earth and deliver the living beings of Kali.

29With the mantra of the Name draw Me down;
I shall [first] cause My mother, father, associates and others to be born.

30Then, drawn by the mantra of the Name [uttered] by you,
I shall take birth on earth together with Baladeva."

31Saying this, Bhagavan disappeared,
and Mahadeva with his associates took birth4.

32Mahavishnu-Sadashiva, the form of Hari-Hara,
was born as Advaita — and the world's distress was gone.

33[…] worshipping Krishna5,
he brought Him to Nadia together with His associates.

34Endless obeisances at the feet of that Advaita Prabhu,
by whose grace we have obtained Gaura Bhagavan!

35I shall describe the life of Advaita briefly;
listen, listen, O hearers, attentively.

36In Srihatta, in the land of Laur, there is [a village] Navagrama,
where Raja Divyasimha lived6.

37His court pandita, of the lineage of the sage Bharadvaja,
named Kuvera Acharya, was praised for his good qualities.

38A pure-minded brahmana, keeper of the sacred fire, performer of sacrifices,
he was descended from the family of Narasimha Nadiyal7.

39In the same village [lived] the brahmana Mahananda Mahashaya,
a supreme pandita, the abode of all virtues.

40His daughter Nabha Devi, a great beauty,
was given in marriage to Kuvera Acharya.

41Mahananda had a family priest, a brahmana,
whom Nabha Devi always called her brother.

42That brahmana took sannyasa from Lakshmipati;
everyone calls him Vijaya Puri8.

43Advaita Prabhu calls him Durvasa;
it was he who made known Advaita's childhood pastimes.

44Vijaya Puri was a fellow disciple of Madhavendra Puri,
and for that reason Advaita Prabhu greatly honours him.

45What little of Advaita's life I heard from the mouths of devotees
I recalled and wrote down on paper.

46In accordance with that I give my description;
listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind.

47Kuvera Pandita Mahashaya [was like] Kuvera, lord of the yakshas;
as the fruit of his austerities Mahadeva became his son9.

48How this son was born I shall tell in order;
listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind.

49Nabha Devi had six sons and one daughter;
the daughter, as soon as she was born, went to heaven.

50Srikanta, Lakshmikanta, Hariharananda,
Sadashiva, Kushala Dasa and Kirtichandra —

51these six sons went wandering to the holy places;
four died, two came back, missing their father10.

52The two sons, having returned, afterwards took up household life.
Now I shall tell how Srila Advaita was born.

53Grieving for their sons, Nabha Devi and the noble Kuvera
settled in Shantipur on the bank of the Ganga.

54Kuvera Pandita constantly worshipped Narayana;
after some time Nabha showed signs of pregnancy.

55Sadashiva Bhagavan entered the womb.
Some time later Kuvera went to Navagrama

56and met Raja Divyasimha;
he informed the king that Nabha Devi was with child.

57The king said: "Acharya, it seems to me
that through this child the sufferings of living beings will come to an end."

58In due time Nabha's ten months were complete,
and on the seventh day [of the bright half] of the month of Magha Prabhu appeared11.

59Seeing his son, the pandita was overjoyed
and distributed wealth as far as his means allowed.

60Who can count how many musicians came!
At the proper time Kuvera performed the naming ceremony.

61Calling an astrologer, he gave him a name:
one of his names was Kamalakanta.

62Because he is not different from Hari, he was named Advaita ("Non-dual");
under the name Advaita Prabhu became famous.

63Hearing the name of Krishna, Prabhu dances;
receiving the prasada of the shalagrama, he is intoxicated with bliss.

64Thus five years passed;
choosing an auspicious day, his father put chalk into his hand12.

65In a short time he learned much reading and writing;
Kamala played every day with the king's son.

66Hearing the names "Krishna," "Hari," Kamalakanta dances;
the prince, seeing this, mocks him greatly.

67Hearing [the mockery], Kamalakanta roars in anger —
and the king's son falls senseless.

68Seeing this, Kamalakanta runs away;
many people rush to the spot.

69A royal messenger goes and informs the king;
hearing of his son's death, he comes in haste.

70The king sees his son dead, with no consciousness in him;
grieving for his son, the king laments, "Alas, alas!"

71Kuvera Acharya quickly came there;
finding his son who had run away, he learned what had happened.

72Kuvera says: "Why did you kill the king's son?"
Kamalakanta says: "The prince is not dead."

73Hearing this, Raja Divyasimha praises him,
and with the water that had washed the shalagrama's feet [Kamalakanta] revives the prince.

74Seeing this, all the people say: "This mahashaya
must be a portion of Ishvara — know this for certain."

75In this way some time passed;
at the proper time Kamalakanta received the sacred thread.

76Listen, O hearers, to what happened on another day:
Kamala went to the pavilion of Kalika.

77The king and all the people were there;
Kamalakanta, coming there, did not bow to Kali.

78Kuvera Pandita and Maharaja Divyasimha
at once began to speak in anger:

79"O Kamalakanta, what behaviour is this?
You do not bow to the Devi — this is a great outrage!"

80Kamalakanta says: "The Devi will not accept [my] obeisance:
I am Sadashiva — know this for certain."

81Hearing his son's words, the pandita grew angry;
seeing his father's anger, Kamala bowed to the Devi.

82As soon as he bowed, Kalika disappeared,
and the moment the Devi disappeared, the image split apart13.

83The king and all the people were amazed:
"What a wondrous deed of Kamalakanta!"

84Kuvera Pandita says: "Listen, Maharaja:
install another image of the Devi without delay."

85Sri Kamalakanta says: "Listen, O king:
you are a worshipper of Shakti — worship Shakti.

86You always revile the devotees of Vishnu;
for that offence Shakti has left you.

87Always serve the devotees of Vishnu,
and worship the Devi, O king, with devotion.

88When the Devi is gracious, you will become a Vaishnava,
you will leave worldly life, and all offences will go."14

89Saying this, Kamalakanta departed,
and the king installed [images of] the Devi and Vishnu.

90Meanwhile Kamalakanta, having studied grammar,
after some time came to Shantipur.

91There, as he wished, he studied literature, poetics, philosophy and the rest,
the smritis, the Vedas and the Puranas.

92He brought his mother and father to Shantipur
and always served the feet of his mother and father.

93Near Shantipur is the village of Phullavati15;
[there lived] a most excellent pandita named Shantacharya.

94With him the Vedas and the Bhagavata,
the yoga-shastras, the Yoga-vasishtha and the rest

95Kamalakanta studied and received the title of Acharya;
by expounding bhakti he made the title Acharya meaningful.

96Listen, O hearers, to a wonder that happened during his studies.
Next to the Ganga was a very deep lake (bil),

97full of fragrant lotuses;
countless snakes, hooded and unhooded, swarmed there.

98Seeing those lotuses, Shantacharya Mahashaya
became eager to worship his chosen Deity with them.

99Understanding his teacher's wish, Advaita
quickly brought many lotuses from the lake:

100he walked on the water as on dry land.
Seeing this, Shantacharya was astonished to the core.

101He thinks: "Advaita is not a human being at all;
it seems to me he is a portion of Ishvara."

102Having finished his studies, Advaita came home;
after some time his mother and father left this world.

103Advaita went to Gaya to offer the pinda
and gradually travelled to all the holy places.

104In the south he met Madhavendra Puri;
[Advaita] heard from him the whole truth of bhakti.

105He studied the scriptures of bhakti with Madhavendra;
grieving for [the sufferings of] living beings, Madhava Puri meditates on Krishna.

106Madhava says: "Advaita, you are Sadashiva;
bring Krishna and save the living beings of Kali.

107See: the whole world is devoid of devotion to Krishna;
give the living beings devotion to Krishna and deliver them.

108You will bring Krishna to the earth —
I saw this in a dream and tell it to you."

109Advaita says: "Puri Gosani, give me this blessing:
that Krishna may come and deliver the living beings."

110Advaita stayed some days with Madhavendra,
and from there afterwards went west.

111In Kashi he met Vijaya Puri;
wandering on, he then came to Vrindavana.

112He circumambulated the whole land of Vrindavana;
one night he saw a dream:

113dark as a fresh cloud, enchanting the worlds,
Hari with a peacock feather, the flute at His lips,

114wearing yellow cloth, with ankle bells on His feet,
His body dazzlingly radiant, full of the nectar of rasa,

115stands in His threefold-bending pose.
Seeing this, Advaita Prabhu rose up trembling

116and fell at Sri Krishna's feet, stretched out like a rod.
Krishna says: "Advaita, you are Shiva Gopeshvara16.

117Restore the lost holy places, preach bhakti,
give the living beings Krishna-Hari-nama and deliver them.

118There is an image of Mine named Madanamohana
in a grove on the bank of the Yamuna.

119On account of robbers I am hidden;
dig up the earth and raise Me up.

120Manifest My service and do good to the world."
Saying this, Bhagavan disappeared.

121Having seen the dream, Advaita woke and sat up;
when the night was over, he went and found [the place].

122Having performed his morning duties, he brought people
and raised Madanamohana from the grove.

123With great labour they dug out the Deity;
seeing Him, all the people of Vraja were enchanted.

124Performing the abhisheka, [Advaita] installed the Thakura
and appointed a well-conducted Vaishnava brahmana for His worship.

125Advaita Prabhu went to circumambulate [Vraja].
Hearing [of the Deity], the mlecchas came to break the Thakura.

126On account of the yavanas, Thakura Madanamohana became [little] Gopala
and hid beneath the flowers17.

127All the mlecchas entered the temple,
searched, did not find the Thakura, and went away.

128When the yavanas had gone, the pujari came;
not seeing the Thakura in the chamber, he was grieved.

129From people he heard of the yavanas' outrage
and, striking his head, wept without end.

130When Advaita Prabhu came in the evening,
[the pujari] cried out: "The mlecchas have taken the Thakura!"

131Not seeing the Thakura, Advaita wept bitterly;
in anguish of heart he lay down without food.

132At the end of the night Bhagavan says to Advaita:
"Wary of the mlecchas, I am hiding beneath the flowers.

133Having become Gopala, I lie beneath the flowers;
take Me and place Me inside the temple.

134Offer Me fruits and roots,
and you yourself, having taken prasada, sleep in peace.

135Everyone will see Me as before;
proclaim [My] name — Madana-gopala."

136In great bliss Advaita Prabhu began to dance;
he brought the Thakura to the temple to offer Him food.

137Having offered fruits and roots,
he laid Madana-gopala on His bed.

138Having taken prasada, Advaita lay down to sleep;
rising in the morning, he went to the bank of the Yamuna.

139On the bank of the Yamuna he saw that brahmana
and told him: "Go quickly to the temple."

140The brahmana says: "Why should I go to the temple in vain?"
Advaita says: "Go and see — Krishna is there."

141The brahmana hurried to the temple
and saw Madana-gopala.

142The joy of that brahmana cannot be described:
he offers praises and obeisances and rolls on the ground.

143From that time this Lord Madanamohana
is called Madana-gopala by everyone18.

144One day in a dream Madanamohana
spoke these words to Advaita:

145"In Mathura there lives a Chaube brahmana;
he is My exclusive devotee.

146The Chaube and his wife are full of devotion;
in parental love (vatsalya) they always cherish Me.

147They constantly think of Me as their son;
I shall surely fulfil their desire.

148Their son's name is Madanamohana;
with him I shall spend some time.

149When Rupa and Sanatana come to Vrindavana,
I shall leave the Chaube.

150In the morning that devotee, the Chaube, will come here;
give Me to him and do not grieve."

151Advaita says: "Hari, if You leave me and go —
I tell You truly — I shall lose my life."

152Bhagavan says: "Advaita, listen to one thing:
here there is an image of Mine non-different [from Me] —

153the form that Sri Vishakha made;
all sing of it as 'Vishakha's picture.'

154Seeing that form, Sri Radha swooned;
the picture is My image, a Deity non-different [from Me]19.

155Take that picture-image to Shantipur
and worship it, calling it Madana-gopala."

156Saying this, Bhagavan disappeared.
Waking, [Advaita] sees that the night has turned to dawn.

157At that moment a Chaube brahmana came
and began to tell of his dream that night:

158"This Thakura came to my house last night,
woke my wife, calling 'Mother, mother!',

159and called me: 'Father, listen to what I say:
I am with Advaita — bring Me here.

160You two are My mother and father;
bring Me and care for Me in every way.'"

161Hearing this, Advaita prostrated himself [and said]:
"Take this Madanamohana and go."

162In great bliss the Chaube took Madana-gopala
and served Him for a long time as his son.

163Meanwhile Sri Advaita Prabhu began to wander [through Vraja]
and in a certain grove found the picture-image.

164Having obtained the image, he floats in the waters of the ocean of prema;
after some time he came to Sri Shantipur.

165In Shantipur he installed that image,
and the name Madana-gopala became known.

166Advaita in Shantipur meditates on Gopala's feet;
by providence Madhavendra Puri came there.

167Seeing the image of Sri Krishna, he bowed down;
Advaita came there.

168Advaita honoured Srila Madhavendra
and again and again prostrated himself before him.

169From him he received initiation in the ten-syllable Gopala mantra;
all say Advaita is a disciple of Madhavendra.

170Having stayed some days in Shantipur,
Madhavendra Puri set out for the south.

171From the south Madhava brings sandalwood from the Malaya hills
to relieve the heat of Govinda's body.

172Coming to Remuna, he saw Gopinatha,
who out of love for him stole sweet rice;

173out of love for him Gopinatha is called Kshira-chora.
Endless obeisances at the feet of such a Madhavendra!

174Having given the sandalwood to Gopinatha by Govinda's order,
Madhavendra set out for the land of Vrindavana

175and, meditating on Sri Govinda's lotus feet,
having manifested bhakti, he left this world20.

176Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear what I shall now tell.

177By Advaita's order that Raja Divyasimha
installed images of Kali and Vishnu and worshipped them.

178By remembering Sri Vishnu his sins were destroyed;
that king came to Shantipur,

179surrendered himself at Advaita's feet
and, giving up the Shakti mantra, took initiation in the Gopala mantra.

180Advaita gave him the name Krishnadasa;
it was he who made known something of Advaita's life21.

181Having studied the Sri Bhagavata with Advaita,
he set out for Vrindavana as a mendicant.

182Krishnadasa Brahmachari became famous in Vrindavana;
Rupa and Sanatana loved him.

183This mahashaya became a resident of Vrindavana;
his friendship with Kashishvara Gosvami was very great.

184He went to Vrindavana before everyone else;
all proclaimed him "Vrindavanavasi"22.

185Thus I have told of Krishnadasa Pandita;
now listen to what I shall say.

186A brahmana of the strictest conduct named Bada Shyamadasa,
learned in many shastras, the abode of all virtues,

187would go to whatever land he heard of a pandita
and defeat all the panditas in debate.

188Everywhere he gained the name of "conqueror of the quarters" (digvijayi);
one day he came to Advaita in Shantipur.

189Entering into debate, he was defeated
and saw Advaita as Sadashiva himself.

190Bada Shyama received the Krishna mantra from Advaita
and began to study the scripture Sri Bhagavata.

191In the Bhagavata he became a supreme scholar;
he is known in the world by the name Bhagavata Acharya23.

192Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall tell of Srinatha Acharya.

193Srinatha Chakravarti, foremost among panditas —
some call him Srinatha Acharya.

194He studied the Bhagavata with Sri Advaita Prabhu,
and Sri Advaita Prabhu gave him initiation.

195He is a branch of Sri Chaitanya, an object of His grace;
his pupil is the poet Karnapura, son of Shivananda.

196In Kumarahatta he installed the Deity of Krishna-raya
and wrote the commentary on the Bhagavata, the Chaitanya-mata-manjusha24.

197Now hear the account of Brahma-Haridasa:
how he was brought up in a yavana's house.

198For the sin of stealing the calves, Brahma Mahashaya,
becoming the ward of a yavana, lost his caste.

199He was born in Budhana, in a brahmana family,
and became a yavana through the fault of [eating] yavanas' food25.

200In infancy his mother and father died;
a yavana came and took him to his own house.

201The ruler of Anduya26, named Malaya Kazi —
he was brought up by him and ate his food.

202Haridasa constantly remembers his past sin;
one day he came to Sri Shantipur,

203took shelter at the feet of Advaita Prabhu
and studied the scriptures of bhakti with him.

204He received initiation from Advaita;
day and night he chants three hundred thousand names of Hari:

205a hundred thousand Hari-namas in the mind, a hundred thousand he hears with his ears,
a hundred thousand names he sings aloud in sankirtana.

206Seeing him intoxicated with Hari-nama, [he was named] Haridasa;
noble brahmanas come and bow to him.

207The supreme Vaishnava Haridasa Mahashaya,
having become a renunciant, always worships Sri Krishna.

208A digvijayi pandita named Yadunandana
one day came to Haridasa.

209There was a debate with him on the truth of God,
and Yadunandana was defeated in every respect.

210[Haridasa,] refuting the doctrine of knowledge, established the primacy of bhakti,
and Yadunandana accepted that teaching.

211At that time Sri Advaita Prabhu came there;
bowing down, Yadunandana says: "You are the Lord.

212Give me initiation [in the mantra] of Krishna and deliver me."
Sri Advaita Prabhu agreed.

213Srila Yadunandana Acharya Mahashaya,
becoming a disciple of Advaita, teaches the Bhagavata.

214Yadunandana's disciple is Dasa Raghunatha,
who became famous as Dasa Gosvami27.

215The glory of Sri Haridasa is boundless:
he is expert in bhajana, his conduct accords with the shastras.

216Sri Advaita Prabhu feeds him the shraddha offering (shraddha-patra);
all people say: "This is an impure act."28

217Hearing the people's censure, Advaita says to Haridasa:
"Show a little of your power."

218Hearing this, Haridasa took away fire:
for a whole day no one could obtain fire.

219The brahmanas and all the people [came] to Advaita
and say: "In what land shall we get fire?"

220Advaita Prabhu says: "I have no fire;
Brahma-Haridasa has hidden the fire."

221All together went to Haridasa,
prostrated themselves and offered many praises.

222Haridasa mercifully took a tuft of grass,
blew on it — and kindled fire.

223All say: "Haridasa is not a human being at all;
he is the lord Brahma himself — know this for certain."

224From Shantipur Haridasa Mahashaya
came to the village of Phulia.

225In that village [lived] an excellent brahmana named Ramadasa,
a supreme pandita endowed with all virtues.

226He conceived firm devotion for Haridasa;
becoming his disciple, the brahmana purified his mind.

227Many noble brahmanas of the village of Phulia
took shelter at Haridasa's feet.

228By Haridasa's power many residents of Phulia
became Vaishnavas and float in love of Krishna.

229From Phulia Haridasa went to Kuliya29
and began austerities in a great forest.

230A snake and a tiger lived in that place;
they listened to Haridasa's Hari-nama.

231Hearing the Name, the snake and the tiger began to dance
and, liberated, both went to Vaikuntha.

232From there Haridasa came to Shantipur
and settled in solitude on the bank of the Ganga.

233Many brahmanas and panditas of Shantipur
reviled Advaita in an assembly.

234All say: "He fed a yavana the shraddha offering —
let no one have even a sesame seed's worth of contact with him!"

235Unworthy brahmanas and panditas reject Advaita,
while worthy brahmanas and panditas stand on Advaita's side.

236The brahmanas of Shantipur split into two parties:
some for Advaita, some against.

237All the brahmanas opposed to Advaita
gathered at a single invitation [to a feast].

238Those brahmanas saw Haridasa:
his form was radiant, his sacred thread gleamed30.

239The radiant thread shines brightly on his body,
the splendour of his body seems to outshine the sun.

240Brahma-Haridasa in the dress of a sannyasi —
with joy in their hearts they insistently bring him.

241All say: "Best of svamis, accept our invitation."
Haridasa says: "I eat [only] Vishnu's prasada."

242The brahmanas say: "We shall offer food to the shalagrama;
we shall seat you in the middle and all eat."

243Haridasa accepted the invitation
and ate together with the brahmanas.

244Having eaten, the brahmanas performed achamana;
at that moment Advaita Prabhu arrived.

245Haridasa fell at Advaita's feet;
Advaita says: "Haridasa, you are here?"

246Haridasa says: "Everyone insisted so much —
that is why I accepted the invitation."

247All the brahmanas, bowing at Advaita's feet,
say: "We are unworthy.

248Forgive the offence, Prabhu, be merciful to all;
knowing us to be ignorant, Prabhu, give us the shade of your feet."

249The great Sri Advaita Prabhu
satisfied all the brahmanas with sweet words.

250Having performed this pastime in this way,
Haridasa went from Shantipur to Navadvipa.

251Seeing Haridasa, the kazi had him bound:
"Why, being a yavana, do you practise the Hindu religion?"

252Haridasa says: "Religion is service to Hari;
what you see as the religion of the yavanas is nothing."

253Hearing this, the kazi grew very angry
and had him locked up in prison.

254In prison [Haridasa] performs sankirtana with the prisoners;
the kazi in anger binds Haridasa tightly,

255ties him in a sack and drowns him in the Ganga;
seeing this, all the people lament, "Alas, alas!"

256Ten or twenty days later, in a fisherman's net
that Haridasa came up — all say: "Treasure!"

257They brought that sack and gave it to the yavana ruler;
cutting it open, they see Haridasa in the sack,

258seated in yoga posture, chanting Hari-nama.
All the yavanas came and bowed to him:

259"Not knowing your nature, we committed an offence;
best of sannyasis, be merciful, grant us your favour."

260Haridasa says: "No one is guilty of any offence:
whatever is the will of Ishvara, that is what everyone receives."31

261Having shown mercy to the yavanas, Haridasa
went and arrived at Benapol on the bank of the Ganga32.

262There he sat in solitude and practised austerities;
a prostitute sent by the kazi came there33.

263The prostitute was of the Mughal race34, a great beauty:
whoever sees her loses his composure.

264The ascetic loses his austerity, the yogi his yoga;
from a beautiful woman's glance one's reason is lost.

265Adorned with all kinds of ornaments,
she went before Haridasa and said:

266"O sannyasi Thakura, listen to my words:
tonight I shall spend with you."

267Haridasa says: "I agree:
when [my] Hari-nama is finished, I shall keep your company."

268Hearing this, the prostitute was very pleased;
with Haridasa's Hari-nama the night turned to dawn.

269Haridasa says: "The night has turned to dawn;
tonight your company will surely be granted."

270In this way three or four nights passed;
by the sight of the saint the prostitute's sins were destroyed.

271As it is said: "Not the holy places made of water, nor the gods made of clay and stone [alone purify]: they purify after a long time, but saints by their mere sight."35

272The prostitute says: "There is no such man in the three worlds,
who blows away with a breath a woman's company freely offered!"

273The prostitute says: "Prabhu, you are a great mahajana;
what honey do you drink? Give [it to me too].

274Having drunk that nectar, you [merely] make me dance attendance;
mercifully let me too drink that nectar."

275Haridasa says: "Listen to my words:
that wealth is gained by giving up wealth and honour."

276The prostitute says: "I shall distribute my wealth
and come to take shelter at your feet."

277That prostitute had heaps of wealth;
she distributed it, choosing worthy people.

278Having distributed her wealth, she came to Haridasa;
Haridasa says: "There are still ornaments on your body.

279Give up your costly ornaments and clothes,
give up your lovely tresses."

280Hearing this, the prostitute cut off her tresses
and gave all her clothes and ornaments to the poor.

281Having bathed and put on white clothes,
she came and fell at Haridasa's feet.

282[Haridasa said:] "The body on which you wore ornaments
shall now be adorned with wood and clay."

283He had her apply tilaka on twelve places [of the body];
on her neck was a necklace of tulasi wood.

284Tying a shikha on her head, he gave her Hari-nama:
"In this Name there is honey; drink it."

285*"Sweeter than the sweet, the most auspicious of all auspicious things,
the fruit of the creeper of all the Vedas, a wish-fulfilling tree —
the name of Krishna, chanted even once, with faith or with neglect,
O best of the Bhrigus, delivers any human being."*36

286"With faith always chant the Name:
when your sins are destroyed, you will find nectar in the Name."

287Having said this and delivered the prostitute, Haridasa
went from there on pilgrimage to the holy places.

288Seeing the prostitute's renunciation, the kazi Mahashaya
thinks: "Haridasa is not a human being at all.

289I meant to destroy his virtue and sent a prostitute,
but by his power the prostitute became a Vaishnavi."

290Haridasa Mahashaya is Brahma, the creator of the world:
for the sin of stealing the calves he became a yavana.

291The sage Richika had a son named Brahma;
by his father's curse he became a yavana.

292Richika told his son to bring tulasi;
he brought unwashed tulasi and gave it into his father's hand.

293In anger the sage Richika said to his son:
"For this offence you will be born in a low family."

294By his father's curse Richika's son, Brahma Mahashaya,
merged with Brahma, the creator of the world, and became Haridasa.

295Prahlada came and joined with them:
the three, united, [became] the great Sri Haridasa37.

296Why Prahlada became a yavana —
listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind.

297One day Prahlada was engaged in the worship of Krishna;
the four Sanas, Sanaka and the others, came there.

298The daityas, bowing to the four Sanas,
seated them and honoured them with water for the feet and arghya.

299Having honoured them, they informed Prahlada,
but Prahlada, absorbed in the worship of his Deity, heard and did not hear.

300The rishis waited for some time
and with heavy hearts went away from there.

301Through this Prahlada committed an offence against Vaishnavas38:
he became intoxicated with tamo-guna, and calamity followed.

302He insulted Indra and the other gods,
and showed respect neither to Brahma nor to Shiva.

303Intoxicated with tamo-guna, he was disrespectful;
then Prahlada went to Vaikuntha.

304Where Narayana [dwells] with Lakshmi and Sarasvati,
there came Prahlada, intoxicated with tamo-guna,

305and without greeting Him says to Narayana:
"Sit on a low seat; I shall sit on the throne."

306Saying this, Prahlada sat on the throne.
The wise say this happened because of Prahlada's offence against Vaishnavas.

307Showing mercy to Prahlada, Lord Narayana
remembered the four Sanas and the gods.

308As soon as He remembered them, all appeared there,
praised Bhagavan and bowed down.

309Seeing the four Sanas, Prahlada Mahashaya
was freed from tamo-guna, and his memory awoke.

310Prahlada says: "I have committed a great offence:
you came to my house, and I did not receive you.

311There is no one as fallen and sinful as I;
forgive my offence, be merciful, O Gosanis."

312Saying this, Prahlada fell flat like a rod
at the feet of the four Sanas and remained lying on the ground.

313The four Sanas say: "There is no offence on you:
by seeing you we attain Krishna's feet.

314By your grace Krishna remembered us,
and we have seen both a saint like you and Krishna."

315Prahlada's offence was gone and his heart was fulfilled;
he honoured the assembly of rishis and the assembly of gods.

316Narayana says: "Prahlada, in the age of Kali
you will take birth on earth and become a yavana.

317Becoming Haridasa, you will increase the glory of the Name;
I shall take birth in the form of Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

318When, born in a low family, you chant the Name,
the seed of your offence will be destroyed."

319That Prahlada joined with Brahma-Haridasa,
while in another manifestation Vidhi (Brahma) became Gopinatha Acharya39.

320Gopinatha is a disciple of Advaita, a branch of Chaitanya.
I have written briefly of Haridasa's nature.

321Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall tell of Advaita's marriage.

322Near Saptagrama is a village named Narayanapura;
many brahmanas live there.

323Kulinas, shrotriyas and kapas live there;
the kapa Nrisimha Bhaduri also lived there40.

324The kapa Nrisimha Bhaduri is Himalaya,
and his wife is surely Menaka.

325He had two daughters — Sri Sita Thakurani:
the elder is Sita, the younger Sri Thakurani.

326Sita is Yogamaya, Durga, Bhagavati;
her manifestation is Sri Devi — know this for certain41.

327Nrisimha's wife, leaving the two daughters,
departed this world — so I have heard from people.

328[Nrisimha] thinks about the marriage of his two daughters, now grown up;
in a dream he sees Advaita as the husband of both.

329In the two daughters he sees the very nature of Bhagavati,
and in Advaita he saw the form of Sadashiva himself.

330Having seen the dream, he put his two daughters in a boat,
keeping in mind: "I shall go to Shantipur."

331He arrived at the ghat of Kuliya,
and there met Bada Shyamadasa Acharya.

332He had a long conversation with Bada Shyamadasa
and told Bada Shyamadasa of his dream.

333Bada Shyamadasa went to Advaita,
wishing to arrange the marriage.

334Bada Shyamadasa says: "Prabhu, marry."
Prabhu says: "Who will give [a daughter] in marriage to an old man like me?"

335From Kuliya Nrisimha came to Shantipur
and met Advaita Prabhu at the ghat.

336Advaita met Sri Sita —
husband and wife were able to recognise each other.

337Sita Devi and Sri Devi say to Bhaduri:
"Give us both to Advaita."

338On an auspicious day Nrisimha Bhaduri
gave his daughters to Advaita in the town of Phulia.

339The rulers of that land, the two brothers Hiranya and Govardhana,
dearest disciples of Yadunandana Acharya42,

340bore all the expenses of the wedding,
and the rite was performed with great pomp.

341Advaita Prabhu married Sri Sita.
I shall tell of a pastime on the day of the pakasparsha43:

342Sita came with a dish of rice into the row [of diners];
a wind arose and forcefully blew away her head-covering.

343With the dish in both hands, she cannot hold the cloth:
with two other hands she pulls the cloth over her head.

344All the brahmanas saw her four-armed;
Sita quickly withdrew the two hands.

345Thus I have told of Sri Sita's marriage;
Advaita lived as a householder with his two wives.

346Formerly Advaita's school (tol) was in Nadia;
after marrying he established his school in Shantipur.

347Sita Devi and Sri Devi from Advaita
[received initiation] with great joy in their hearts44.

348Five sons were born of Sita Devi,
one son was born of Sri Devi.

349The eldest, Achyutananda, is Ganesha;
the gopi Achyuta entered into him.

350His manifestation is Chhota Shyamadasa Mahashaya;
Sita loves him like a son.

351With motherly love Sita nursed him at her breast;
the wise Chhota Shyamadasa sees Mother Sita four-armed.

352Krishnadasa Mishra, Gopala, Balarama,
Svarupa, Jagadisha — these are the five sons45.

353Srila Krishnadasa is Karttikeya;
Gopala, Balarama, Svarupa and Jagadisha are his manifestations.

354Sita Devi had two maidservants, Jangali and Nandini;
Sita herself initiated them in the Krishna mantra.

355Nandini serves the feet of Sri Sita,
while Jangali went to a forest to perform austerities.

356Jangali lives in that jungle
in the company of tigers, bears and other beasts.

357The ruler of Gauda went hunting in that forest
and saw a supremely beautiful woman.

358The woman, in the dress of an ascetic, performs austerities;
the king conceived the intention of destroying her chastity.

359Coming near, he sees — a man!
Great doubt arose in the king's mind.

360The king says: "Ascetic, are you a woman or a man?"
Jangali says: "I am a woman, not a man.

361Women see [in me] a woman, men a man;
never do I call anyone a man46.

362Good people always see me as a woman
and address me: 'Mother, mother.'

363A man at first sees me as a woman;
when his mind turns wicked, he sees a male form."

364The king brought women and made a test:
the women saw [her] female form.

365At the king's order a man came at once
and, examining, saw male marks.

366The king says: "Mother, I am a great offender;
give me the dust of your feet and save me."

367Jangali showed the king great mercy,
and the king built her a dwelling there.

368Everyone calls that place Jangali-tota.
Thus I have made known the power of Jangali47.

369Listen, listen, O hearers, attentively:
pay heed to what I shall now tell.

370A disciple named Ishana says to Advaita48:
"Tell me, Mahashaya, how will the living beings be liberated?

371— said Ishana. — You married and became a householder,
but you have not done what would deliver the living beings."

372Hearing this, Advaita roars:
"I shall bring Krishna with His associates to Nadia!"

373Saying this, Advaita Prabhu began austerities
and brought Krishnachandra with His associates to Nadia.

374Having come, Prabhu preached the doctrine of bhakti
and through bhakti-yoga delivered the whole world.

375Mahaprabhu shows Advaita the devotion due to a guru
and every day takes the dust of his feet.

376At this the Lord of Shantipur is greatly pained:
his mind is always downcast, he finds no peace.

377Advaita says: "I shall go against bhakti:
I shall constantly expound the Yoga-vasishtha and the like.

378Now I shall preach the doctrine of knowledge,
so that anger will be kindled in Prabhu.

379Hearing of it, Prabhu will surely come to Shantipur
and punish me with His own hand."

380Resolving thus in his mind, Advaita,
abandoning dualism, propounds the doctrine of knowledge49.

381He instructs his disciples in the doctrine of knowledge;
hearing this, Prabhu became angry at heart.

382Hearing [of it], Nityananda and Sri Gauranga Raya
in great anger hurry to Shantipur.

383Hearing the doctrine of knowledge, Prabhu blazed up like fire,
beat him with His own hand and threw him to the ground.

384Advaita says: "Prabhu, You are the guru of the world,
the wish-fulfilling tree that fulfils the desires of devotees."

385Saying this, he bowed at Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu embraced him and held him to His heart.

386Prabhu says: "Those who have accepted the doctrine of knowledge —
make them now followers of bhakti."

387Advaita preached the doctrine of bhakti to all his disciples;
giving up the doctrine of knowledge, all practised bhakti.

388Kamadeva Nagara, Agala and Pagala,
and also Shankara did not give up the doctrine of knowledge50.

389Shankara says: "We are followers of the doctrine of knowledge:
without the doctrine of knowledge no one will attain perfection."

390Advaita says: "Give up the doctrine of knowledge."
Shankara says: "If you can defeat [us] in debate,

391then we shall give up the doctrine of knowledge and accept bhakti;
otherwise no one has the power to make us give it up."

392Advaita says: "Shankara, you have become a baul (madman);
by your teaching all people will become aul (confused)51.

393Being obstinate against your guru, you have become offenders:
never will you attain perfection."

394In anger Advaita rejected them;
rejected, they went off to other lands.

395Those whom Nitai, Chaitanya, Advaita and the devotees rejected
are counted as "tyagi" (rejected).

396Those whom the devotees of Krishna call guilty
are great "tyagis" — know this for certain.

397Those offenders whose offence does not go
are shown to be the foremost of all the rejected.

398Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall tell of Madhava, Advaita's disciple.

399I [have already] told Madhava's life briefly as best I could;
in describing his sannyasa I repeat myself52.

400The noble Durgadasa of Srihatta
came with his wife to Nadia and settled there.

401He had two sons, abodes of virtue:
the elder was Sanatana, the younger was named Parashara.

402This brahmana Parashara was a great devotee of Kali,
and everyone called him Kalidasa.

403Under the name Kalidasa he became known;
his son Madhavadasa became an excellent pandita.

404When Prabhu manifested the Mahaprakasha in Srivasa's house,
Madhavadasa was there at that time.

405Madhava heard Hari-nama from Prabhu's mouth,
and his heart no longer wished to remain in worldly life.

406From Navadvipa he moved to Kuliya
and day and night meditated on Chaitanya's lotus feet.

407He studied the shastras with Sri Advaita
and became known in the world as Madhava Acharya.

408The Tenth Canto of the Sri Bhagavata
he set out in songs in various metres,

409named the book Sri Krishna-mangala,
and in Sri Kshetra offered it at Chaitanya's feet.

410Taking something also from other Puranas,
he added it to the Krishna-mangala.

411Having read the book, Mahaprabhu showed him mercy
and had Sri Advaita Prabhu give him initiation.

412Later he became famous as Kavivallabha Acharya;
the world proclaims him "the Vyasa of Kali."

413He is counted in the group (yutha) of Vishakha;
Madhava's siddha name is the sakhi Madhavi.

414Madhava received all of Advaita's grace,
and the desire arose in him to become a sannyasi.

415How Madhava became a sannyasi, listen, O hearers:
I shall describe it briefly.

416Sri Krishna Chaitanyachandra came from Nilachala
and arrived in Gauda.

417"I shall go to Vrindavana by the road through Gauda" —
this He announced to all.

418Having come to Gauda, Srila Prabhu Gaura Raya
first goes to Panihati, to Raghava's house.

419From there He went to Kumarahatta
and took His meals in the house of Srivasa Pandita.

420From there, having stayed in the houses of Vasudeva and Shivananda,
Prabhu went to Shantipur.

421He took His meals in the house of Advaita Acharya,
and from there went to Kuliya.

422He arrived at the house of Madhava Acharya
and stayed seven days in his house53.

423For all seven days the residents of Navadvipa
gaze at Gauranga, floating in an ocean of bliss.

424The joy of Madhava cannot be described:
Madhava sinks and surfaces in the ocean of bliss.

425Great is Sri Chaitanya's mercy to Madhava:
because of his devotion the Magnanimous One stayed seven days.

426Who can describe how many people
came from Navadvipa through all those seven days!

427Having shown mercy to the residents of Navadvipa,
Gauranga Sri Hari set out for Vrindavana.

428Mahaprabhu showed mercy to Rupa and Sanatana
and turned back from Kanai Natashala.

429Seeing the crowds of people, He did not go to Vrindavana
and quickly went to Nilachala.

430By the forest road Mahaprabhu went to Vrindavana —
Krishnadasa Kaviraja has described it in detail.

431Hearing that Prabhu had gone to Vrindavana by the Jharikhanda road,
Madhava became very dejected.

432Hearing that Prabhu had come back from Vrindavana to Nilachala,
Madhava's mind went mad.

433Madhava's heart is not bound to worldly life;
seeing this, Madhava's mother weeps aloud.

434To keep him at home,
Madhava's mother hastily began arranging his marriage.

435Seeing his mother's preparations,
Madhava then fled and went to Vrindavana.

436He took sannyasa from Paramananda Puri
and learned bhajana from Rupa and Sanatana54.

437Grieving for her son, his mother gave up her life;
hearing of it, Madhavadasa came to Shantipur,

438and then by way of Kheturi went again to Vrindavana
and single-mindedly practised the sadhana [of service] to Radha and Krishna.

439Madhava Acharya loves me very much;
I write his life with love in my heart.

440Whatever comes to mind at any time, that I write down;
may the devotees not hold the repetitions against me.

441Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear what I shall now tell.

442[There was a] Vaidika [brahmana] of the lineage of the sage Vatsya named Vishuddha Mishra; his son Madhu Mishra made his home in Srihatta.

443In the village of Baraganga, where brahmanas lived,
Madhu Mishra married and stayed in that village.

444In time four sons were born to him, foremost among panditas:
Upendra, Rangada, Kirti[da] and Kirtivasa55.

445Upendra Mishra's wife was named Kamalavati;
seven sons were born to her, foremost among panditas:

446Kamsari, Paramananda and Jagannatha,
Padmanabha, Sarveshvara, Janardana, Trailokyanatha.

447Jagannatha received the title of Mishra Purandara;
coming to the bank of the Ganga, he settled in Navadvipa.

448Jagannatha Mahashaya is Nanda, the king of the cowherds,
and Vasudeva came and joined in him56.

449A resident of Srihatta named Chandrashekhara
became known by the name Acharyaratna.

450He settled on the bank of the Ganga;
in his house Gauranga danced in the mood of the Devi.

451A resident of Srihatta, Nilambara Chakravarti,
lives in Nadia on the bank of the Ganga.

452His house is in the village of Belpukhuria;
two sons and two daughters were born to him.

453The first was Yogeshvara Pandita, the second Shachi,
the third Ratnagarbha Acharya, the fourth is called Sarvajaya57.

454Everyone sings of Shachi Devi as Yashoda;
as a [further] manifestation Sri Devaki is merged in her.

455Mishra Purandara married Shachi,
Sri Chandrashekhara marries Sarvajaya.

456Eight daughters were born of Shachi and died;
at last Vishvarupa was born.

457Baladeva was born as Vishvarupa;
he received initiation from Ishvara Puri.

458Vishvarupa's younger brother is Nimai Pandita,
known in the world by the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

459The son of Ratnagarbha Acharya was named Lokanatha;
Vishvarupa resolved to take him along.

460As soon as he wished it, Lokanatha came to him;
taking him, Vishvarupa went to the south.

461Having taken sannyasa, [Vishvarupa received] the name Shankararanya Puri;
his maternal cousin Lokanatha became his disciple58.

462Lokanatha serves Vishvarupa;
by providence Ishvara Puri arrived there.

463Vishvarupa bowed to Ishvara Puri
and placed his own divine power in Puri.

464As it is said in the Chaitanya-chandrodaya-nataka, in the words of Kali: "His elder brother, who took no wife — Lord Sankarshana, Vishvarupa on earth — having, it is said, placed his own splendour in Ishvara Puri, having earlier taken to the wandering life, disappeared."59

465Vishvarupa says: "Lord, this concentrated power —
give initiation to Nityananda and place it in him."

466Saying this, Vishvarupa attained perfection (left the world),
and Ishvara Puri went from there to another place.

467In Rarh there is a village called Ekachaka;
in it lived [a brahmana] named Sundaramalla Nakadi Banduri.

468His son Mukunda was known as Hadai Ojha;
the name of Hadai Ojha's wife was Padmavati.

469Hadai Pandita is a manifestation of Vasudeva,
Padmavati in another manifestation is Devaki.

470Seven sons of great virtue were born to them;
I shall tell their names — listen attentively:

471Nityananda, Krishnananda and Sarvananda,
Brahmananda, Purnananda and Premananda,

472Vishuddhananda — these are the seven sons60.
The eldest of all, Nityananda, is Balarama.

473Vishvarupa and Nityananda are one being (svarupa):
Baladeva, through difference of manifestation, appears in two forms.

474Nityananda also had another name, Chidananda;
Hadai Ojha gave it at Advaita's order.

475In household life he was known as Nityananda,
in sannyasa his name is Nityananda Avadhuta.

476Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear what I shall now tell.

477In the village of Ekachaka Prabhu Nityananda Raya
always played with bliss in his heart.

478A certain sannyasi sees a dream:
Balarama comes and speaks these words to him:

479"I am the son of Hadai Ojha, O best of sannyasis;
in this incarnation My name is Nityananda.

480Give Me initiation, have Me accept sannyasa,
and keep for Me the name Nityananda Avadhuta."

481Saying this, Balarama spoke a mantra into his ear:
"This is the mantra you are to give Me."

482Saying this, Balarama disappeared;
waking, the best of sannyasis sees that the night has turned to dawn.

483By providence that sannyasi came to Hadai Ojha's house
and asked for Nityananda-svarupa as alms.

484That sannyasi's name was Ishvara Puri;
giving Nityananda initiation, he made him a sannyasi61.

485He placed Vishvarupa's power in Nityananda:
in the form of power Vishvarupa merged with Nitai.

486By the power of the sannyasi Nitai became an avadhuta
and travelled to many holy places with Ishvara Puri.

487One day Ishvara Puri said:
"I shall go to seek my guru, Madhavendra Puri.

488You travel to all the holy places
and keep in mind a meeting with Madhavendra."

489Saying this, Ishvara Puri went away from there
and came to Madhavendra Puri.

490Nityananda travels alone to all the holy places;
by providence he met Madhavendra.

491A meeting with Ishvara Puri also took place;
the joy that arose cannot be described.

492Sri Nityananda Raya, with bliss in his heart,
always sees Madhavendra Puri as his guru;

493Madhavendra Puri towards Sri Nityananda
always shows a friend's affection.

494For some days they stayed together in talks of Krishna,
then they went their ways, each wherever he wished.

495Having travelled to all the holy places, Sri Nityananda Raya
set out for Vrindavana with bliss in his heart.

496Wandering through the twelve forests, he searches for Krishna;
again he met Ishvara Puri.

497Bowing down, he says: "Guru, where has Krishna gone?"
Ishvara Puri says: "There where Navadvipa is:

498He has descended in Navadvipa from the womb of Shachi
and performs Krishna-sankirtana to deliver the living beings."

499Hearing this, Nityananda Prabhu went to Navadvipa
and met Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

500I have already described all these matters in brief62;
finding an occasion, I have told them again in detail.

501O hearers, listen with contentment
and do not hold this repetition against me.

502Whatever matters I did not write before,
I have disclosed them in this detailed account.

503Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall describe Prabhu's pastimes in Vanga (East Bengal).

504Vrindavana Dasa has described [them] at length;
what remains I shall describe63.

505From Navadvipa Prabhu came to Vanga
and, joyful at heart, stayed on the bank of the Padma.

506He displays pastimes of learning, [performs] sankirtana of the Name,
and on the bank of the Padma draws Narottama64.

507After staying some days, Prabhu thought:
"I must go to the land of Srihatta.

508Having seen My father's birthplace and My grandfather,
I shall soon come back to the bank of the Padma."

509Thinking thus, Mahaprabhu set out for Srihatta
and arrived at Faridpur on the bank of the Padma.

510From there He went to Nurpur in Vikramapura,
and then visited Suvarnagrama.

511From there He came to the land of Egarasindur —
a most charming town on the bank of the Brahmaputra.

512In that land the village of Betal is well known;
by His grace the Merciful One came there.

513Near it is the village of Bhitadia,
a seat of kulinas famed in many lands.

514There lives the brahmana Lakshminatha Lahiri,
a supreme Vaishnava, surpassing all in virtues.

515In his house Prabhu took His meals
and, because of his devotion, stayed two to four days.

516Lakshminatha says: "Prabhu, from the signs I see
I understand that You are Narayana.

517O merciful Prabhu, be gracious:
knowing me to be fallen, Prabhu, give me the shade of Your feet.

518I have no son — give me the blessing of a son,
that he be a supreme pandita endowed with all virtues,

519a supreme devotee of Krishna, purifying the family,
that by his virtues people's evil tendencies may be destroyed."

520Saying "So be it," Prabhu gave His blessing;
hearing this, Lakshminatha's heart rejoiced.

521By that blessing a son was born — Rupa Narayana65.
Hear, O devotees, the background of Lakshminatha.

522The excellent Padmagarbha Acharya, foremost among panditas —
at the time when he was studying in Navadvipa,

523at that time there was a brahmana resident of Navadvipa,
Jayarama Chakravarti, a man of very good character.

524Knowing [Padmagarbha] to be a kulina, he gave him a daughter
and insisted on keeping him in his own house.

525Living in his father-in-law's house,
he studied for several years in Navadvipa.

526A son of great virtue was born to him;
they gave him the name Sri Purushottama.

527Leaving his wife and son in his father-in-law's house,
Padmagarbha, eager to study, set out for Mithila.

528Having studied nyaya and other shastras in Mithila,
he went with a joyful heart to Kashi.

529There he studies sankhya and the rest, mimamsa, vedanta,
and with utmost eagerness studies the Vedas and other [scriptures].

530The guru of Madhavendra Puri, named Lakshmipati,
lived in Kashi for a long time.

531That Padmagarbha Acharya, foremost among panditas,
received initiation in the Gopala mantra from Lakshmipati.

532That Padmagarbha Acharya, the best of Krishna's devotees,
composed a commentary on the Krama-dipika,

533wrote a commentary on the Paingi-rahasya-brahmana,
and composed a dualist commentary on the Upanishads66.

534Having finished his studies, the noble Padmagarbha
settled in his birthplace, Bhitadia.

535Coming to Bhitadia, he married twice more,
and many sons were born — Lakshminatha Lahiri and others.

536Purushottama with his mother became a resident of Navadvipa;
a treasury of virtues, he became a dear devotee of Chaitanya.

537Purushottama became very learned in many shastras;
all know him by the title of Acharya.

538Seeing Chaitanya's sannyasa, he became as if mad,
went to Varanasi and took sannyasa.

539In sannyasa his name is Svarupa Damodara,
Prabhu's most intimate devotee, an ocean of rasa.

540If anyone brings a song, a book or a verse,
Prabhu hears it [only] after Svarupa has examined it.

541His guru is Sri Chaitanyananda;
with him he studied Vedanta and other shastras.

542The half-brother of that Svarupa Gosvami
is Lakshminatha Lahiri — listen, all you hearers67.

543That Lakshminatha is a devotee and foremost among panditas;
for four days Prabhu rested in his house.

544Having blessed Lakshminatha, Prabhu Gaurahari
after some days came to Srihatta.

545Prabhu arrived at the village of Baraganga
and bowed to His grandfather, Upendra Mishra.

546From the introduction he learned it was his grandson;
His grandmother came there too.

547Prabhu bowed to His grandmother
and rested there for some days.

548There Prabhu performed a wondrous deed,
and seeing it His grandfather was amazed.

549Upendra Mishra, in order to copy the Chandi,
had collected many palm leaves.

550Prabhu is sitting near His grandfather;
Upendra Mishra writes the first verse on a palm leaf.

551Then Upendra Mishra's wife came
and took Upendra Mishra into the inner apartments.

552She says: "My lord, I have seen a wonderful dream:
this son of Jagannatha is Narayana Himself."

553Mishra says: "Dear, this is true:
in His appearance and nature are the signs of Ishvara."

554Kamalavati says: "My lord, to tell this dream
I have called you to a private place."

555Mishra says: "Dear, do not disclose this;
feed Gauranga with devotion."

556Saying this, Upendra Mishra went to the outer apartments
and saw the Chandi copied out in full.

557"Jagannatha's son Gaura is Ishvara Himself:
otherwise who could copy the Chandi in a moment?"

558Thinking thus, Upendra Mishra Mahashaya
took Gauranga into the inner apartments.

559His grandmother gave Him a sweet jackfruit;
Prabhu ate it and was very pleased.

560His grandmother says: "Child, You are Narayana:
You appeared to me in a dream.

561That sweet form remains fixed in my heart;
show me, show me that form — let me see it again."

562Showing mercy to His devotees, Prabhu Gaura Raya
shows the two of them His sweet form.

563Seeing the form, both steadied their minds
and, assuming the bodies of associates, went to the eternal abode68.

564Having shown mercy to His grandmother and grandfather,
Sri Gauranga Raya goes to the bank of the Padma.

565Staying there, Prabhu displays pastimes of learning,
performs sankirtana of the Name, manifests His power.

566The people of Vanga are very fortunate:
men and women together sing sankirtana.

567Prabhu showed great mercy to the people of Vanga,
and all understood that Gaura is Ishvara Himself,

568Svayam Bhagavan Krishna — how could it be otherwise?
Hearing this, the great sinners are pained at heart.

569All those who are averse [to the Lord] do not accept Chaitanya
and establish their own divinity.

570All people are devoted to Sri Chaitanyadeva
and constantly sing of Him as Ishvara.

571Seeing this, some great sinners
each establish their own divinity.

572Proclaiming themselves Ishvara,
in the guise of Krishna they ruin people, going about Rarh and Vanga.

573A brahmana named Vasudeva, a great villain,
commits great outrages in Rarh, the sinner.

574He says: "I am Ishvara, Gopala, the son of Nanda";
hearing this, all people call him "Shiyal" (Jackal).

575This great sinner was rejected by Mahaprabhu
and disowned by Mahaprabhu's devotees.

576Another sinner, a kayastha named Vishnudasa,
displays "his power" in Vanga.

577He says: "I am Raghunatha, [come] from Vaikuntha,
appeared on earth to deliver the world.

578Hanuman, Angada and all the lords of monkeys —
all are my devotees, as everyone knows."

579The villain ruins people with all kinds of tricks;
he got the name "Kapindri" ("Monkey-lord").

580This Kapindri was rejected by Mahaprabhu
and disowned by Mahaprabhu's devotees.

581A brahmana named Madhava, the pujari of a certain king,
stole the ornaments of the Sri Vigraha,

582went off somewhere to a cowherds' settlement
and began serving as priest to the milkmen.

583The lustful sinner, dressing there as "Chudadhari" ("the crest-wearer" [like Krishna]), has himself sung of as Krishna-Narayana.

584He says: "I, Chudadhari, am Krishna-Narayana:
whoever worships me will go to the abode of Vaikuntha."

585The cowherd men and women are wholly under his sway;
with the cowherd men and women he constantly dances and sings.

586Dressed as "Chudadhari," he plays "pastimes" with the milkmaids,
and so became famous under the name Chudadhari.

587With the women of chandalas and other low castes,
under the pretext of Krishna's lila, he has relations.

588One day Madhava, taking women with him,
came boldly to Nilachala.

589Madhava, dressed as Chudadhari, together with the women
came to Mahaprabhu's sankirtana.

590Prabhu says: "What Chudadhari is this who has come,
playing 'pastimes' with women, destroying dharma?

591O devotees, this Chudadhari has fallen from dharma:
whatever land he lives in, that land will be ruined.

592Do not look upon the face of this fallen offender;
drive him quickly out of Purushottama."

593Hearing this, the devotees drove him out,
and Chudadhari fled to Vanga69.

594Wicked men who think themselves Ishvara the servants of Yama
will make suffer in hell as long as the moon and sun [shine].

595The sinner who calls anyone but Sri Chaitanyachandra Ishvara
will go to hell.

596In the Chaitanya-bhagavata Sri Vrindavana Dasa
has revealed this in the form of a brief sutra.

597As it is said in the Chaitanya-bhagavata70:
*"From time to time certain sinners come
and ruin people by making them accept themselves [as God].
To fill their bellies, all these sinners —
one calls himself Raghunatha;
another great sinner, abandoning Krishna-sankirtana,
has himself sung of as Narayana.
How many ghosts have themselves sung of:
abandoning Krishna-sankirtana — the singing of ghosts!
I have seen day after day what becomes of them;
with what shame does that wretch have himself sung of?
In Rarh there is yet another brahma-daitya (brahmana-demon):
inwardly a rakshasa, a brahmana only in dress;
that sinner calls himself Gopala —
therefore all call him 'Shiyal' (Jackal).
Whoever calls anyone but Sri Chaitanyachandra Ishvara
is base, worthless and to be pitied."*

598Having searched out all the deeds of these wicked ones,
I have disclosed them along with their names, having received my guru's order.

599This has become a gloss and commentary on the sutra of Vrindavana [Dasa]:
let no one ever associate with the rejected.

600Through association with the wicked everything people have is destroyed;
the rejected are never fit for association.

601As it is said in the Sri Bhagavata: "One should never associate with the wicked who satisfy only the genitals and the belly: whoever follows such a one falls into blind darkness, like a blind man led by the blind."71

602These wicked men perform the rasa and similar pastimes,
which the Sri Bhagavata forbids.

603As it is said in the Sri Bhagavata: "One who is not a controller should never do this even in thought: whoever does it out of folly perishes, as [one other than] Rudra [would perish by drinking] the poison born of the ocean."72

604Dressed as Chudadhari, [this] sinner went with low-caste women
and became an outcaste (apankteya) for brahmana society.

605Whoever accepts gifts from low castes and eats their food,
or goes with a low-caste woman —

606[doing so] unknowingly falls, and knowingly becomes equal to them:
this is seen in the law-book of Manu.

607As it is said in the Manu-smriti: "A brahmana who has gone with women of chandalas and low castes, eaten [their food] and accepted [their] gifts, falls if unknowingly, and if knowingly becomes equal to them."73

608The pujari Madhava Chudadhari is a sinful soul74;
hear more about him, honoured hearers.

609He calls himself Krishna, has the ghosts sing of him:
abandoning Krishna-sankirtana — the singing of ghosts.

610Singing "tiger songs," he goes from house to house75
and, dressed as Krishna, seduces low-caste women.

611He is a disciple of Jackal Vasudeva;
the wicked man was born in the vamshaja family of Bandyaghati of the Shandilya gotra.

612Thus I have briefly told of Prabhu's pastimes in Vanga;
now I begin to describe Nityananda's marriage.

613One day Prabhu Nityananda Rama says:
"I shall marry — listen, devotees."

614Pandita Krishnadasa Hod in joy
brings Nityananda to his house in Dogachhia.

615A worry arose in their minds: who will give [a daughter] to a sannyasi?
At that moment Uddharana Datta arrived,

616the best of devotees, Uddharana Datta of the goldsmith-merchant [caste],
whose food cooked in ghee Nitai eats.

617Uddharana says: "The noble Suryadasa Sarakhel
has two very beautiful daughters.

618When I learned of the intention to marry,
I went to Suryadasa.

619When I made the proposal of marriage,
Suryadasa at once flared up in anger.

620By Prabhu's power Suryadasa will become softer than clay:
manifest your power in proper fashion."

621In such conversation the day passed;
the next day Suryadasa Sarakhel came.

622Prabhu says: "This is King Kakudmi76;
I shall marry his two daughters."

623Coming there, Suryadasa bowed to Nitai
and began to tell his dream:

624"I saw in a dream Balarama-Nityananda:
He entered into union with my two daughters.

625I gave Him both daughters,
and the daughters, receiving a sannyasi as husband, were content."

626Having told the dream, Surya rejoiced
and took Nityananda Rama to Shaligrama.

627Arriving home, they see that a daughter has died:
a venomous snake has bitten her.

628Seeing his dead daughter, Surya weeps;
smiling, Nityananda gave her back her life.

629That daughter's name was Vasudha,
and her younger [sister] is called Jahnava.

630[Suryadasa] gave both daughters to Nityananda;
Suryadasa, [formerly] of low kula, gained honour77.

631By Nityananda's grace he became respected in brahmana society;
becoming Nityananda's disciple, he made his family glorious.

632Vasudha [Prabhu] took in marriage according to the rite,
and the younger, Jahnava, Prabhu accepted as dowry78.

633Marriage for a sannyasi is forbidden by the shastras,
but by the will of Rama-Nityananda it came to pass.

634A sannyasi who becomes a householder is called "one who keeps the cat's vow,"
and a sannyasi who knows a woman is certainly an "avakirni."

635One who falls from lifelong brahmacharya (naishthika)
has no atonement: he is counted as fallen.

636The virtuous do not perform sacrifice, study, marriage and the like with him;
whoever touches him must perform the chandrayana vow.

637As said by Hemadri in the Shraddha-kalpa, [quoting] Yama:
"Whoever, having entered the ashrama of the yatis, falls back from it again, destroying the dharma of the yati — that vow is called 'the cat's vow.'"
In the same place, Devala:
"One under a vow who approaches a woman is called an avakirni."79

638[In] Shankara's commentary on the Brahma-sutra: "But in both cases [they are] outside, according to smriti and custom. Whether the falling of those vowed to chastity from their ashramas be a great sin or a minor one, in both cases they must be kept outside by the virtuous. 'One who, having taken up the naishthika dharma, falls from it again — for that slayer of the self I see no atonement by which he might be purified'; 'having touched a brahmana fallen from his vow, one expelled from the circle [of the community], one who has hanged himself or one bitten by worms, one should perform the chandrayana' — because of these and similar smritis condemning [them] most strongly, and because of the custom of the virtuous. For the virtuous do not perform sacrifice, study, marriage and the like with them."80

639A dog that eats [its own] vomit is called "vantashi" ("eater of what is vomited");
a sannyasi who has become a householder is surely like it.

640Therefore all call him "vantashi";
his offspring too bear the taint of "vantashi."

641The virtuous shun them all:
far from marriage, they are not even fit to be touched.

642Humans and others are tainted by such faults,
but in one favoured by Ishvara no fault arises.

643As it is said in the Sri Bhagavata:
"For the mighty it is no fault, as for fire, which consumes everything."81

644What more can be said of Ishvara Himself!
He has no connection at all with maya or with what is born of maya.

645Rama-Nityananda is Ishvara Himself:
injunctions and prohibitions have no relation to Him82.

646His offspring are portions of Ishvara, gurus of the world,
protectors of the world, wish-fulfilling trees.

647Although the fault of "vantashi" is not in them,
still the kulacharyas vainly call [them] "virabhadri."83

648Nityananda Prabhu, taking Vasu and Jahnava,
lived joyfully in Khardaha.

649First seven sons were born to Nityananda;
from Abhirama's obeisances all seven died.

650The last son is Virabhadra, named Virachandra,
a vyuha of Sankarshana, whose abode is the Milk Ocean.

651A daughter named Ganga was born — [the goddess] Ganga Devi;
the daughter too did not die from Abhirama's obeisance.

652Abhirama dances and says: "[He] is a portion of Ishvara;
the world will be delivered — I know it for certain."84

653Prabhu Virabhadra is an avatara of Ishvara;
by his mercy the world was delivered.

654Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear what I shall now tell.

655Saptagrama, Shiludi and Sitahati,
Nanyapur, Jhamatpur and Naihati —

656all these villages are on the bank of Sri Ganga,
all these villages lie near Katwa.

657A resident of Nanyapur is Bhagiratha Acharya [of the] Chatta [family];
now hear his background, O best of devotees.

658Aravinda's son was Ahita, his son was Dvakara,
Dvakara's son was Chattamanu Mahashaya.

659Chattamanu's son was Duryodhana,
his son Chand Chatta, his son Tapana.

660His son was Haridasa Chatta Mahashaya;
his son's name is Gauridasa.

661Gauridasa's other name is Bhagiratha;
by many wives many children were born to him.

662Ramachandra, Mahesha, Krishna are the children of one wife;
Shiva and Vishveshvara, two, another wife bore;

663Srinatha and Sripati were born of a third wife;
Srinatha has the title of Ghatakacharya.

664I have already told of Madhava Chatta:
Madhava is Bhagiratha's adopted son85.

665Srinatha's mother raised him;
Madhava became Srinatha's third brother.

666Madhava became Bhagiratha's beloved son;
Nityananda gave him his daughter Ganga.

667Marriage of a disciple with his guru's daughter is forbidden by the shastras,
but by Nityananda's order it came to pass.

668As it is said in the Mahabharata, in the Adi-parva: "As [Kacha] was departing for the abode of the gods, Devayani said this: 'Take my hand according to the rite, with mantras.'"

669Kacha said: "You, good lady, are by dharma always to be honoured by me as my guru's daughter: as your father Shukra, my guru, is ever to be honoured by me, so are you, Devayani; you should not speak to me thus. Considering you my guru's daughter, I refuse — not because of any fault [in you]."86

670In the Matsya-sukta: "[Marriage] is forbidden with [those of] the same pravara, with the offspring of a disciple and with the offspring of the guru who gave [the knowledge of] Brahman."87

671The greatness of Ishvara cannot be understood:
by the will of Ishvara the impossible comes to pass.

672In Nanyapur is the house of Bhagiratha Chatta;
Madhava Acharya went and lives in Nanyapur.

673Madhava Chatta is tainted by the fault of "virabhadri,"
and moreover by marriage to his guru's daughter.

674Seeing these and other faults, Devi[vara] Mahashaya
proclaims Madhava a kulina of the Khardaha mela.

675By Devi[vara]'s order he became a foremost kulina;
his sons later pass over to Dasharatha:

676in the mela of Dasharatha Ghataki they became kulinas;
compared with Khardaha, [the mela] of Dasharatha is lower88.

677Madhava settled in Nanyapur,
staying at times in Khardaha.

678In Nanyapur many kulinas live —
a most charming place, an abode of panditas.

679Madhava lives in Jirat and Balagarh,
and sometimes rests in Katwa.

680Hear, O hearers, of Madhava's nature:
in him King Shantanu and Madhuspanda united;

681a manifestation of the sakhi Madhavi also joined him —
the three, uniting, have now become Madhava Pandita89.

682Through another manifestation of Madhavi there is another Madhava Pandita,
who composed the songs of the Sri Krishna-mangala.

683Of that Madhava I have already told:
he is a disciple of Advaita and a favourite of Mahaprabhu.

684Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear what I shall now tell.

685One day Virabhadra, in order to receive initiation,
set out for Shantipur, to Advaita.

686Putting musicians and many people into a boat,
he goes joyfully to receive a mantra.

687Hearing the music, Sri Jahnava
asked Abhirama the reason.

688Abhirama says: "Virabhadra Mahashaya
is going to Shantipur, to Advaita's house:

689with the hope in his heart of receiving initiation
Virabhadra has set out with great pomp."

690Then Sri Jahnava said to Abhirama:
"Bring Virabhadra back at once.

691Let him go to Shantipur with his mother's permission —
tell Vira this, Abhirama."

692Receiving the order, Abhirama hurries;
the noble one sees the boat moving away swiftly.

693Calling and calling, he could not turn the boat back,
and with a shout he hurled his flute at the boat.

694From the blow of the flute the boat split and sank;
all the people swam ashore.

695Having swum ashore, Virabhadra says:
"Why did you break the boat, Rama Mahashaya?"

696Abhirama says: "Listen, Prabhu Vira:
go to Shantipur with your mother's permission.

697Bow to your mother and, taking her permission,
go to Shantipur and receive the mantra from Advaita."

698Hearing this, Prabhu Virabhadra was ashamed:
"To go without telling my mother is improper."

699Saying this, Virabhadra goes to his mother;
Srila Jahnava Devi is engaged in worship.

700At that moment there was no cloth on her head,
when her grown son Virabhadra came.

701With joined hands Jahnava Ishvari offers prayers,
and with two other hands draws the cloth over her head.

702Seeing her four-armed, Vira prostrated himself fully
and bowed down, rolling long on the ground.

703Vira says: "Mother, give me initiation;
I shall no longer go to Shantipur for initiation."

704Hearing this, Jahnava gave him initiation.
Thus I have described Prabhu Vira's initiation90.

705Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall tell of the appearance of the image of Sri Shyamasundara.

706Virachandra Gosani Prabhu is an avatara of Ishvara;
all his efforts are for the deliverance of living beings.

707Giving Hari-nama, he delivers fallen people,
making no distinction between Hindu and Muslim.

708Seeing his power, people are amazed.
One day he went to the gate of the padishah of Gauda.

709All say: "Huzur, this is a wise pandita,
he knows great fakir-craft, he is a great fakir."

710The padishah with great courtesy
joyfully gave him a seat.

711The padishah says: "You are a good fakir;
eat in my house today."

712Hearing this, Prabhu Virabhadra smiles softly:
"By eating in a yavana's house a Hindu loses his caste.

713But if you give me your own dish,
I shall surely eat it — this I tell you."

714Hearing this, the padishah laughed:
"Cook, bring the dish quickly!"

715Receiving the order, the cook brings an excellent dish,
tied up in a clean cloth.

716The Gosani says: "Quickly untie the dish."
The cook untied it — the padishah sees flowers:

717jati and yuthi jasmine, malati, bel, bakula,
roses smeared with sandal — and swarms of bees come.

718In this way the dish was brought three times,
and each time they saw all kinds of flowers in it.

719The padishah says: "The Gosani is the foremost of fakirs;
Thakura, take whatever gift you wish."

720The Gosani says: "A precious stone, the 'teluya stone,'
adorns your gate, glittering.

721I wish to take it" —
says the Gosani — "with it I shall have a beautiful Deity carved."

722The padishah prised out the stone and gave it to Virachandra;
taking the stone, Vira went to Khardaha.

723From that stone he had the image of Shyamasundara carved;
seeing it, all people were freed from all their sorrows.

724He held a great festival and invited the Vaishnavas;
all the associates of Chaitanya came.

725Advaita's son, the merciful Sri Achyutananda Mahashaya,
performed the installation and abhisheka of the image.

726All these matters I have recorded
in great detail in the Virachandra-charita91.

727From the stone left over after carving Shyamasundara
two charming images were carved:

728the image of Sri Nanda-dulala resides in Svamibana,
and in Vallabhapura Vallabhaji is installed92.

729Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall describe Virabhadra's marriage.

730A resident of Jhamatpur, Sri Yadunandana,
had two very beautiful daughters:

731the elder Srimati, the younger Narayani,
blessed in beauty, virtue and character, enchanting the world.

732That fortunate brahmana, of the Pippali family,
gave both daughters to Prabhu Virabhadra.

733In the Virachandra-charita I have described
this wedding in great detail with joy in my heart93.

734Virachandra has one daughter and three sons;
I shall tell all their names:

735the eldest is Gopijanavallabha, the middle Ramakrishna,
the youngest Ramachandra, excellent in every way.

736The daughter's name is Bhuvanamohini;
her husband is Parvatinatha Mukhuti of Phulia.

737Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear what I shall now tell.

738[There was] a shrotriya brahmana named Ratneshvara;
he had two daughters, great beauties.

739One daughter he gave to the kulina Hari Mukhuti,
the other daughter he gave to the vamshaja Sarvananda Banduri.

740Hari's son was called Yogeshvara Pandita,
Sarvananda's son was called Vidyadhara.

741Vidyadhara's name later became Devivara;
it was he who divided the kulinas according to their "faults."

742Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall describe something of these events.

743One day Yogeshvara, wandering about,
comes at midday to Devivara's house.

744Devivara was elsewhere at that time;
Yogeshvara went and bowed to his aunt.

745His aunt says: "Son, bathe quickly:
the meal is ready, as you see."

746Yogeshvara says: "Auntie, it is not fit to say,
but if I eat your rice, the honour of my kula will be lost.

747We are kulinas, and you are lower in kula;
if I eat your rice, my kula will be diminished."

748Saying this, Yogeshvara took his leave,
and Devivara's mother began to weep.

749Yogeshvara went away from there,
and then Devivara arrived.

750Bowing to his mother, Devivara says:
"Why are you weeping, mother? Tell me everything."

751His mother says: "Son, it is not fit to say:
if a nephew eats his aunt's rice, he loses his caste!

752Yogeshvara, my sister's son, came here;
he did not eat and spoke harsh words to me.

753Yogeshvara said: 'Auntie, you are lower in kula;
if I eat your rice, my kula will be diminished.'"

754Saying this, Yogeshvara, without eating,
went away to his own house.

755Hearing this, Devivara said to his mother:
"We are not kulinas — that is why Yogeshvara did not eat."

756In anger and grief Devivara's mother rebuked her son:
"What need had I of a bad son like you?

757If Yoga falls at my feet and eats my rice —
if you accomplish this, son, then I shall call you son.

758O Vidyadhara, I have suffered humiliation;
I tell you truly: I shall not live."

759Devivara says: "Mother, do not worry at all:
by your grace, mother, everything will be accomplished."

760Saying this, Devivara went to perform austerities
and received the desired blessing from the Devi.

761The Devi says: "Listen, listen, O Vidyadhara:
here is the blessing you desire:

762whatever you say of anyone within twelve dandas94,
that will come true — know this for certain."

763By the Devi's blessing Vidyadhara received the name Devivara ("blessed by the Devi");
he determined the honour of the families according to their "faults."

764Having received the blessing, Devi[vara] investigates the families:
he sees the kulinas "sunk in evil deeds" (ku-karye lina)95.

765In the great kulinas he sees faults, great and greater:
"By the faults I shall firmly fix the kulas."

766He sees that many kulinas, full of faults,
have become "unfit" (achala) in society.

767Having searched out all the great faults,
he established the kulas according to the faults.

768By what faults he established kulinism —
some of this I shall show.

769Srinathai Chatuti had two daughters;
they went to Dhandha ghat to fetch water.

770A Muslim named Hasai Khandar
violated the chastity of both daughters96.

771One daughter is married by Paramananda Putitunda,
the other daughter is married by Gangavara Bandya.

772This Devivara calls the fault of "dhadha."
Now I shall tell of the fault of "nadha."

773The Banduris of Nadha were vamshajas;
Manohara Mukhuti married there

774and for that reason became a vamshaja;
[but] Devivara abolished his vamshaja status.

775A vamshaja is an enemy of the kula, unfit to sit with in a row;
by his touch the shraddhas and other rites for the ancestors are spoiled.

776The original vamshajas were without the Vedas;
they are counted as non-brahmanas, and [connection with them] diminishes the kula.

777Those brahmanas who associated with them
were counted among the vamshajas.

778O hearers, listen attentively:
now I shall tell how vamshaja status was abolished.

779To preserve Manohara's kulinism,
Devi[vara] makes the Banduris of Nadha "mashachatakas":

780they became shrotriyas [of the rank of] "masha-chataka";
this Devivara called the fault of "nadha."97

781Shivacharya, nephew of Gangananda Mukhuti,
married a saptashati girl from Mulukjuri and became rejected.

782This Devivara calls [the fault of] "mulukjuri."
[Now] about the fault of "virabhadri" — listen, honoured hearers.

783The offspring of a sannyasi are called "vantashi";
this fault is imputed to Nitai's offspring as well.

784All know that Hadai Pandita was a vamshaja,
