and all know that his gain (the "village" designation of the family) is Bandyaghati.

785These two faults are known under the name "virabhadri";
the ghatakas ceaselessly speak of the fault of "virabhadri."98

786Nityananda's daughter was married by Madhava Chatta,
Virabhadra's daughter was taken by Parvati Mukhuti.

787To preserve their kula,
Devivara calls Virabhadra "Batavyal."

788Prabhu Virabhadra's son, Srila Ramachandra,
sits in Devivara's assembly like Indra himself;

789seeing this, [Devivara] calls Virabhadra "Batavyal" —
that is why Ramachandra became a Batavyal.

790Prabhu Gopijanavallabha and Ramakrishna
never came to Devivara's assembly:

791they remained vamshajas with the gain Bandyaghati.
[Thus arose] these two [designations], Batavyal and Banduri99.

792Through the faults of "nadha," "dhadha," "mulukjuri," "virabhadri" and others
Devi[vara], laughing, created the Phulia mela.

793Garagari, Pippalai and Dingsai —
[of them] I inform the kulinas that they are vamshajas.

794By accepting gifts from the unworthy and officiating for those unfit,
they became outcastes — all know this.

795By giving their daughters to kulinas they become shrotriyas,
but for true kulinas they remain unfit to sit with in a row.

796Yogeshvara's father, Hari, took a daughter of Garagari,
Yogeshvara marries a daughter of Pippalai.

797Madhu Chatta marries a daughter of Dingsai;
receiving the fault of "dindi," Madhu became tainted.

798Previously Dingsai had not given daughters to kulinas;
Madhu Chatta was the first to marry [his daughter].

799Therefore Madhu Chatta became unfit in society,
and Yogeshvara Pandita gives him a daughter.

800By these and many other faults Devi[vara] proclaims the Khardaha mela,
whose original root is Yogeshvara Pandita.

801Remembering his mother's words, the ghataka Devivara
loudly pronounces this verse in the assembly:

802"If a hare had horns, if there were a flower in the sky, if a barren woman had a son — then Yogeshvara would have kula (or: then Yogeshvara has no kula)."100

803Devivara, keeping in mind the [double] sense, "kulam" and "akulam,"
cleverly keeps the promise [made] to his mother.

804Hearing the verse, Yogeshvara — as if thunderstruck —
hurries and falls at his aunt's feet:

805"Auntie, feed me [even] water-soaked rice101;
ask Devi[vara] and save my kula."

806Hearing Yoga's words, his aunt was pleased
and, calling [her son], told him to give Yogeshvara kula.

807Hearing his mother's words, Devi[vara] said, laughing:
"Then the meaning is 'Yogeshvara has kula.'"

808Devivara kept his promise to his mother,
and by his aunt's grace Yogeshvara obtained kula.

809Devivara's tantric guru, Chatta-Shobhakara,
sits in the assembly on a high seat:

810"I am Devivara's guru, the eldest of all;
seeing me, Devi[vara] will make [me] the highest."

811Seeing [such] impropriety, Devi[vara] grew angry;
no virtuous brahmana was pleased.

812Devi[vara] divided all the kulinas according to their faults:
seeing whose faults were alike, he divided them into thirty-six melas.

813Having finished the work within twelve dandas,
he cast his eyes on his guru Shobhakara.

814Devivara made Shobhakara "without kula,"
and by Shobhakara's curse Devi[vara] was left without descendants.

815Shobhakara and Devivara are guru and disciple;
hear now, O hearers, the words of both.

816Calling out, Devivara says: "Shobhakara is without kula!"
Calling out, Shobhakara says: "Devivara is without descendants!"

817"Shobhakara without kula, Devivara without descendants" —
these words spread through the assembly.

818When these words had been spoken in the assembly,
the assembly broke up, and all went to their homes.

819Devivara conceived a hatred for Shobhakara
and came to take shelter at Virabhadra's feet.

820Seeing [the truth of] Vaishnava dharma and hearing the shastras,
Devi[vara] received initiation [in the mantra] of Krishna from Virabhadra.

821Having become a Vaishnava, Devi[vara] said again and again:
"There is no dharma higher than Vaishnava dharma."102

822Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear the genealogies of Advaita and Nityananda.

823Narayana Bhatta, of the Shandilya gotra, was versed in the four Vedas (chaturvedi);
his son is Adivaraha, as all know.

824His son is Vainateya, his son Subuddhi;
[the son] of Subuddhi is Vibudhesha, his son Guha.

825Guha's son is Gangadhara, his son Suhasa,
his son Shakuni, who studied all the shastras.

826His son Maheshvara became a kulina;
his son is Mahadeva, expert in the shastras.

827Mahadeva's son is Tiku, his son Nengura;
Nengura has many sons, excellent panditas:

828Ganga, Soma, Sidhu, Lakhai, Mihira.
Mihira gave his daughter to a vamshaja:

829his kula was lost, he became unfit in society.
Mihira's son is Bhaskara, a mighty pandita.

830All called him a vamshaja;
no one ate with him.

831Bhaskara's son was named Pushkara;
his son Srishtidhara, his son Maladhara.

832Maladhara's son was named Vrishaketu;
his son is Chandraketu, know this for certain.

833Chandraketu's son was named Sundaramalla Nakadi Banduri;
his son is Hadai Ojha, named Mukunda.

834His son is Nityananda, who is Balarama;
his son is Virabhadra, the abode of all virtues.

835Thus I have told the genealogy of Nityananda103.
Now hear the genealogy of Sri Advaita.

836Gautama of the Bharadvaja gotra was versed in three Vedas (trivedi);
his son is Vibhakara, expert in the shastras.

837Vibhakara's son was named Prabhakara;
his son is Vishnu Mishra, the abode of all virtues.

838His son is Kakutstha, foremost among panditas;
his son is Gopinatha, knower of all the shastras.

839Gopinatha's son is Gunakara Vachaspati;
his son is Akashavasi, another name Akai.

840His son is Narayana Panchatapa;
his son is Vardhamana Agnihotri.

841His son is Prithvidhara Kulapati;
his son is Sharabha Acharya, another name Marara.

842Sharabha Acharya's son is Matta Ojha,
another name Matanga Ojha — know this for certain.

843Matanga's son is Jihmani, another name Jaimini;
his son is Bhaskara, a Vedantist, very learned.

844From him the Varendras are reckoned; he was a skilled pandita;
in Ballala's assembly his sons and grandsons [became] kulinas and shrotriyas.

845Bhaskara's son is Sayana Acharya Mahashaya;
his son is Aro Ojha, whom they call Aruni.

846Aro's son is Yadunatha Pandita Mahashaya;
his son is Sripati, an excellent pandita.

847His son is Kulapati, his son Ishana,
his son Vibhakara, his son named Prabhakara.

848Prabhakara's son is Narasimha Nadiyal;
everyone always proclaims him the minister of Raja Ganesha.

849He lived in Shantipur;
from the marriage of his daughter the kapas arose.

850He went and settled in Laur in Srihatta,
staying from time to time in Shantipur.

851Narasimha Nadiyal is also called Nadli;
Nadiyal, Naudiyal, Nadli mean the same.

852Narasimha's sons are Kandarpa, Saranga, Vidyadhara,
Mahadeva, Narayana, Purandara, Gangadhara.

853Of the seven sons Vidyadhara was worthy;
Vidyadhara's son is the wise pandita Chhakadi.

854His sons are Kuvera and Nilambara Acharya;
Kuvera's son is Kamalaksha, Advaita Acharya104.

855Kamalaksha, Advaita Prabhu, has six sons:
Achyutananda, Krishnadasa, Gopala, Balarama,

856Svarupa, Jagadisha — these six,
very learned in all the shastras, endowed with great virtues.

857I have described Advaita's genealogy;
hear, O hearers, the genealogy of Gadadhara Pandita.

858Sushena-muni of the Kashyapa gotra was versed in the four Vedas;
his son is Brahmanya Ojha, whom they call Brahma Ojha.

859His son is Daksha, his son Shantanu,
his son Pitambara — know this for certain.

860His son is Hiranyagarbha, his son Sugarbha (?),
his son's name is Vedagarbha.

861His son is Jigani, also called Mahamuni;
some call Jigani Mahamuni by one name,

862others call him Jaganmahamuni.
Mahamuni has two sons, Svarnarekha and Bhavadeva.

863Svarnarekha [became] a Varendra, Bhavadeva went to the Radhis.
Svarnarekha's son is Sindhu, called Sandhyaika Ojha.

864Sindhu's son is Garuda; he has two sons:
Kratu Bhaduri and Matu Maitra.

865All call them Kratu Kaitai and Matu Maitai;
both excellent men received kulinism in Ballala's assembly.

866Kratu Bhaduri is the foremost kulina of Ballala's assembly;
his sons are Sankarshana-muni and Vasudeva Ojha.

867Sankarshana's son is Bhalluka Acharya, Bhasa Ojha;
Bhalluka's sons are Yogesha and the mighty Divakara.

868Divakara, leaving his place, lost the dignity of kulinism:
going to the village of Karanja, he became a shrotriya.

869Yogesha's sons are Pundarikaksha and Kuvalaya;
Pundarika's son is Vishvambhara Acharya.

870Vishvambhara's son is Lakshmipati Acharya;
his son is Brihaspati Acharya, performer of sacrifices.

871His son is the foremost pandita Udayana Acharya,
author of the Nyaya-kusumanjali and other excellent books105.

872Udayana reformed the kula of the Varendras
and introduced the customs of parivarta and karana.

873Udayana settled in the village of Vaniati;
he had numerous offspring.

874By one wife: Bhupati, Bhavanipati, Chandipati,
Gauripati, Rudranipati and Shachipati.

875For disobeying their father's word these six lost their kula:
calling them "kapas," Udayana excluded them from society.

876Thus the kapas first arose.
Of Udayana's other wife Pashupati was born;

877Pashupati, like his father, became a kulina;
he had many sons:

878Jagai, Ghaghai, Khakhaira, Dhakhaira, Bhadai,
Tarunai, Vasudeva Ojha and Uddhai.

879Some call Uddhai Ugramani.
Ghaghai had many sons:

880Kamai, Kumai, Tikai and Hara Chamai,
Suresha, Vardhamana — these six brothers.

881Kamai's sons are Balai, Pitai, Pushpaketana,
Amshuman, Kusumashekhara, Minaketana.

882Balai's sons are Anga, Bhanga and the wise Vilasa;
Vilasa Acharya was very learned.

883The king of Chittagong named Chitrasena
took Vilasa Acharya [to himself] and honoured him.

884Vilasa Acharya became the king's court pandita
and settled in Chittagong, in the village of Beleti.

885In Chittagong a son was born to him;
they gave him the name Sri Madhava.

886Madhava Acharya became a supreme pandita;
Pundarika Vidyanidhi is his best friend.

887Pundarika is the zamindar of Chakrashala;
he has great friendship with Madhava Mishra.

888Madhava's wife was named Ratnavati,
and Pundarika's wife too is called Ratnavati.

889The wives of both became sworn friends by [the water of] the Ganga106,
and all knew of their friendship.

890A son was born to Madhava in Chittagong;
they gave him the names Jagannatha and Vaninatha.

891Leaving Chittagong, Madhava settled in Nadia
and received the Gopala mantra from Madhavendra Puri.

892Pundarika Vidyanidhi has a house in Nadia;
he goes back and forth between Nadia and Chittagong.

893In Navadvipa Pundarika with a joyful heart
received the Gopala mantra from Madhavendra.

894Pundarika and Madhava Mishra, both,
are counted among the branches of Mahaprabhu.

895Another son was born to Madhava in Nadia,
on the new-moon day of Vaishakha.

896They gave him the name Srila Gadadhara —
the best of the associates of Sri Krishna Chaitanyadeva.

897Gadadhara Pandita is the beloved of Gauranga;
his brother is the wise Jagannatha Acharya.

898Jagannatha settled in Nadia;
his son is the noble Nayanananda Mishra.

899[Gadadhara] loves him as a son, regarding him as his brother's son;
in the town of Nadia he gave him initiation in the Gopala mantra

900and entrusted him with the Gopinatha whom he himself served;
Sri Nayana Mishra Gosani was overjoyed.

901After the disappearance of Pandita Gosani
Nayana Mishra went to Bharatpur in Rarh107.

902I have described the genealogy of Pandita Gosani;
now I shall tell of the origin of the Radhis and Varendras.

903To Adishura's sacrifice came five brahmanas;
their descendants are the communities of the Radhis and Varendras.

904In the Kula-ratna (it is said): "Maharaja Adishura, the ornament of the kshatriya race, brought from Kanyakubja to his kingdom five brahmanas: Medhatithi, Kshitisha, Vitaraga, Sudhanidhi and Saubhari — these five brahmanas came for the sacrifice for the birth of a son. Then, by the time of King Ballala, their offspring gradually multiplied and over a long time reached eleven hundred [families]; of these three hundred and fifty [lived] in Varendra and seven hundred and fifty in Rarh; according to the region where they lived, they received in the world the names Varendra and Radhi."108

905There is a race of Ambashtha kshatriyas of the Lunar dynasty;
in it Raja Adishura was born.

906Great were their learning, intelligence and valour,
but through the mother's fault they became the disgrace of the kshatriya race.

907As it is said in the Ushanas-samhita: "One born secretly of a brahmana and a queen is called a bhishak (physician); being born in the anuloma order, he is named an Ambashtha. Observing the commands of an anointed king, let him practise medicine — the eightfold Ayurveda — and follow the dharma set out in the tantras; or let him practise astrology and arithmetic, or bodily labour, live by agriculture or by a craft involving fire; the Ambashthas may also live by military service, [as] those who live by arms."109

908That Raja Adishura is the lord of Gauda;
he had many other dominions as well.

909The eastern bank of the Jahnavi (Ganga) is called Varendra,
the western bank of the Jahnavi is called Rarh.

910The northern bank of the Padma is counted as Varendra,
the southern bank of the Padma is foremost in Rarh.

911The eastern and western banks of the Ganga are known as the kingdom of Gauda;
many brahmana panditas live there.

912In Adishura's kingdom there were many Vaidika brahmanas;
among them were five kulina Kaushikas:

913Svarna-kaushika, Rajata-kaushika, Kaundinya-kaushika,
Ghrita-kaushika and [plain] Kaushika — these five best ones.

914Svarna-kaushika's name is Dhara Narayana,
the brahmana Rajata-kaushika is named Shivashankara,

915Kaundinya-kaushika's name is Janardana,
the brahmana Ghrita-kaushika is called Bhuvaneshvara,

916Kaushika Kalidasa is very learned.
These five brahmanas are foremost among panditas.

917These five brahmanas were the king's court panditas,
and he always showed them great honour.

918Maharaja Adishura had no offspring;
his queen Chandramukhi lamented greatly.

919The king heard the queen's lament
and prepared a sacrifice for the birth of a son (putreshti).

920He had the five court panditas perform the sacrifice,
but it bore not the slightest fruit.

921The local brahmanas did not know the Vedas;
the king became displeased with them.

922One day the queen says to the king:
"Send people to Kanyakubja to bring brahmanas.

923There are many fire-keepers, knowers of the Vedas, there;
bring five brahmanas and have the sacrifice performed with care."

924On the queen's advice Maharaja Adishura
sends people to Kanyakubja without delay.

925The ruler of Kanyakubja was named Chandraketu;
the messengers went, delivered a letter and explained the reason.

926Chandraketu's other name is Virasimha;
this mahashaya was a generous great hero.

927Receiving the letter, Chandraketu, lord of Kanauj,
at once gave five fire-keepers, knowers of the Vedas.

928The five great rishis, residents of Kanyakubja,
at the king's order set out for Gauda.

929From what village, of what name and gotra [each] brahmana was,
versed in how many Vedas — listen, O hearers.

930Kshitisha of the Shandilya gotra is versed in four Vedas;
some say he is from the village of Jambuchatta, others from Dilichatta.

931Vitaraga of the Kashyapa gotra is versed in four Vedas;
all know he is a resident of the village of Kaulani.

932Sudhanidhi of the Vatsya gotra is counted as versed in three Vedas;
he is a resident of the village of Tadita, foremost among panditas.

933Medhatithi of the Bharadvaja gotra is versed in three Vedas;
all know he is a resident of Audumbara.

934The great rishi Saubhari of the Savarna gotra is versed in three Vedas;
he is foremost among panditas, a resident of the village of Mara.

935With the five rishis [the king of Kanauj] gave five servants,
to protect the five rishis and serve them.

936Kshitisha's servant was named Makaranda Ghosh,
Vitaraga's servant was called Dasharatha Basu,

937Sudhanidhi's servant is Purushottama Datta,
Medhatithi's servant was named Virata Guha,

938Saubhari's servant was named Kalidasa Mitra.
These five servants, dressed as warriors, are kshatriyas.

939These five servants, kshatriya-kayasthas110,
went to Gauda together with the five rishis.

940The five great rishis, putting on warriors' dress,
arrived at the palace of Raja Adishura.

941The king heard: "Five brahmanas have come";
but seeing the warriors' dress, he went into his apartments.

942The king thinks: "If they are brahmanas,
why have they put on the dress of kshatriyas?

943If kshatriya warriors have come in disguise to deceive,
then after testing them my mind will be at rest.

944I was born in a kshatriya family of the Lunar dynasty;
after testing them I shall honour their feet."

945The rishis in warriors' dress came to the palace;
the nobles came and honoured their feet.

946The king was informed of the rishis' arrival;
the king thinks: "I shall go later.

947I shall test what sort of brahmanas they are:
having seen their power, I shall then go and meet them."

948Seeing the king's delay, [the rishis] sat in meditation
and understood everything in the king's mind.

949Knowing the king's thoughts, the rishis then
placed their blessing on a dry log:

950as soon as it was placed, the log came to life.
Hearing this, the maharaja came in fear and haste,

951bowed at the feet of the rishis
and honoured them with water for the feet, arghya and water for achamana.

952In [the year] "Vedas (4), arrows (5), nine (9)" — in Shaka 954111 —
the five great rishis came to Gauda.

953The five rishis summoned the king and queen
and before the sacrifice had them perform the chandrayana vow.

954The king and queen performed the chandrayana vow
and, freed from sin, began the sacrifice.

955By the five great rishis the putreshti was performed,
and a son and a daughter were born to the king.

956Having produced the fruit of the sacrifice, the five great rishis
went back to their own land, Kanyakubja.

957[But] they had performed rites for a low kshatriya in a non-Aryan land,
and for that reason their kinsmen excommunicated them all.

958Excommunicated by their kinsmen, the five
came to Gauda with their wives, sons, grandsons and servants.

959With their fathers came Narayana, Sushena, Dharadhara,
Gautama and Parashara.

960Seeing that the five rishis had come with wives, children and the rest,
Raja Adishura rejoiced at heart.

961The maharaja honoured the five
and gave the five brahmanas five villages on the bank of the Ganga.

962The five great rishis in the land of Gauda,
receiving five villages, were overjoyed.

963Kshitisha received the village of Panchakoti,
to Vitaraga Kamakoti was given,

964Sudhanidhi accepted Harikoti,
to the brahmana Medhatithi Kankagrama was given,

965Saubhari accepted Vatagrama;
these five villages lie side by side on the bank of the Ganga.

966After some time came the excellent panditas
Damodara, Daksha, Chhandada, Sriharsha, Vedagarbha;

967and after some more time the remaining sons
came to their fathers.

968The five rishis, having all their sons with them,
began to live in joy.

969Listen, listen, O hearers, attentively:
now I shall tell whose sons were how many, and their names.

970Kshitisha of the Shandilya gotra has seven sons;
now I shall tell their names:

971Damodara, Narayana Bhatta, Sauri, Shankara,
Vishvambhara, Lokaranya and Hiranya.

972Vitaraga of the Kashyapa gotra has twelve sons;
now I shall tell their names:

973Sushena, Daksha, Bhanu Mishra, Kripanidhi Mahashaya,
Indra, Chandra, Mahesha, Rudra, Jiva,

974Harihara, Baladeva and Danava —
very learned in all the Vedas, knowers of all the shastras.

975Sudhanidhi of the Vatsya gotra has seven sons;
now I shall tell their names:

976Dharadhara, Hrishikesha, Chhandada Mahashaya,
Vibhuti, Bhutabhavana, Deva and Kalyana Mitra.

977Sri Maharshi Medhatithi of the Bharadvaja gotra,
foremost among panditas, has eighteen sons:

978Adya, Madhya, Gautama, Vishruta Mahashaya,
Sriharsha, Sridhara, Krishna, Shiva, Durgadasa,

979Ravi, Shashi, Dhruva, Nikara, Pratapa Mahashaya,
Prabhava, Ganesha, Riksha and Vajra.

980Saubhari of the Savarna gotra has twelve sons;
I shall tell their names:

981Ratnagarbha, Parashara, Rama, Vedagarbha,
Vibhu, Soma, Kashyapa, Vasishtha, Kharva,

982Mahatapa, Kirtiman and Danujari;
Karttikeya is the best of all panditas.

983Of the fifty-six sons ten are foremost among panditas;
now I shall tell their names:

984Damodara, Narayana, Daksha and Sushena,
Dharadhara, Chhandada, Sriharsha, Gautama,

985Parashara, Vedagarbha — these ten lords
became masters in all lands.

986In what lands the descendants of the five rishis settled
I am writing down now and making known.

987Damodara's descendants remained in Varendra,
the descendants of Sauri, Vishvambhara and Shankara settled in Rarh.

988The sons of Lokaranya and Hiranya
also settled in Rarh.

989Of three wives twenty-one sons were born to Narayana:
five settled in Varendra, sixteen in Rarh.

990Now I shall make known their names —
who [settled] in Varendra and who in Rarh.

991Adigai Ojha, Adivibhakara,
Adinatha, Adideva, Adibhaskara —

992these five sons of the eldest wife
made Varendra glorious by settling there.

993Adivaraha, Nano, Gupta, Mahamati, Guna, Saha,
Batuka, Shubhakaya, Nikko and Pui112 —

994these ten sons were born of the middle wife.
Rama, Vibhu, Gana, Nipa, Vika, Madhusudana —

995these are the six sons of the youngest wife.
Adivaraha and the others — sixteen — went to Rarh.

996The sons of Sushena, Bhanu Mishra and Kripanidhi
settled in Varendra.

997The sons of Daksha, Indra, Chandra, Mahesha, Rudra, Jiva,
Harihara, Kamadeva and Danava —

998all of them, foremost among panditas,
went to Rarh and settled there.

999The sons of Dharadhara and Hrishikesha
settled in the land of Varendra.

1000Chhandada, Vibhuti, Bhutabhavana, Deva, Kalyana Mitra —
their sons sanctified Rarh.

1001The descendants of Adya, Madhya, Gautama and Vishruta
made Varendra glorious by settling there.

1002Sriharsha, Sridhara, Krishna, Shiva, Durgadasa, Ravi,
Shashi, Dhruva, Nikara, Pratapa, Prabhava,

1003Ganesha, Riksha, Vajra — their descendants
made Rarh glorious by settling there.

1004All the sons of Parashara, Rama and Vibhu
sanctified Varendra by settling there.

1005Ratnagarbha, Vedagarbha, Soma, Kashyapa, Vasishtha,
Mahatapa, Kirtiman, Danujari, the youngest Karttikeya —

1006their sons, eminent in learning and brahmanical worth,
settling in Rarh, made it excellent.

1007Ratnagarbha is the best of all panditas,
the commentator on the Ramayana, the Vishnu Purana and others.

1008From Adishura to the time of Ballala
the descendants of the five great rishis numbered eleven hundred [families]:

1009in Rarh there were seven hundred and fifty brahmanas,
in Varendra three hundred and fifty.

1010Together they are eleven hundred brahmanas from Kanauj;
the local Vaidikas are counted as seven hundred.

1011Under the influence of the [brahmanas of] Kanauj, the local brahmanas
in Ballala's time took the name "Saptashati" ("the Seven Hundred")113.

1012The gotras Shandilya, Kashyapa, Vatsya, Bharadvaja, Savarna —
the brahmanas of Kanauj are pure in these five gotras.

1013The local Saptashati brahmanas do not have these five gotras;
among them [we find] Pancha-kaushika, Maudgalya, Gautama and others,

1014Saukalina, Vasishtha, Parashara, Alambayana,
Jamadagni, Atreya, Angirasa, Katyayana —

1015these and many other gotras exist among the Saptashatis;
the gotras of the Kanauj brahmanas have no place among them.

1016Ballala had thirty-one court panditas:
eleven before the division into Radhis and Varendras, twenty after.

1017Those who [were] before the division into Radhis and Varendras —
their names I shall now recount.

1018Of the Shandilya gotra, these two:
Jayasagara and Vidyasagara, the best of the Mishras.

1019Vidyasagara's other name is Manisagara.
Of the Kashyapa gotra, these two:

1020Svarnarekha and the excellent Bhavadeva Bhatta.
Of the Vatsya gotra, these two:

1021Chaturbhuja Chaturvedacharya, master of the Vedas and Vedanta,
and Damodara Ojha, foremost among panditas.

1022Of the Bharadvaja gotra, two mighty panditas:
Bhaskara the Vedantist and Parashara Ojha.

1023Of the Savarna gotra, these three panditas:
Aniruddha, Gunarnava and Dharai Upadhyaya.

1024At Ballala's order these panditas
made a census of the Vaidikas, of Kanauj and local.

1025The Kanaujis living in Rarh received the name Radhi,
the Kanaujis living in Varendra received the name Varendra.

1026The local Vaidika brahmanas were seven hundred;
they became known by the name Saptashati.

1027In learning and brahmanical worth the Kanaujis were higher;
the Saptashati Vaidikas were lower in honour.

1028The Saptashatis were only knowers of the Sama Veda;
brahmanas knowing the other Vedas were not seen among them.

1029Giving a daughter to a Kanauji,
the Saptashatis considered themselves highly favoured.

1030Ten panditas divided the Radhis and Varendras,
and one pandita composed the genealogies.

1031All this I shall now describe;
hearing it, the hearers will rejoice.

1032Jayasagara Mishra is the foremost of the Shandilyas in Varendra,
Vidyasagara Mishra the foremost of the Shandilyas in Rarh.

1033Svarnarekha Bhatta is the head of the Kashyapas in Varendra,
Bhavadeva Bhatta the head of the Kashyapas in Rarh.

1034Chaturbhuja Chaturvedacharya is the head of the Vatsyas in Varendra,
Damodara Ojha the head of the Vatsyas in Rarh.

1035In Varendra Bhaskara the Vedantist is foremost of the Bharadvajas,
in Rarh Parashara Ojha is foremost of the Bharadvajas.

1036In Varendra Aniruddha Acharya is the head of the Savarna gotra,
in Rarh Gunarnava Acharya is the head of the Savarna gotra.

1037At Ballala's order these ten noble men,
becoming heads each of his own gotra, divided the Radhis and Varendras.

1038After some time Maharaja Ballala,
establishing kulinas among the Radhis and Varendras, made two communities.

1039Jayasagara, Svarnarekha, Chaturbhuja Chaturvedacharya
and Bhaskara the Vedantist are the best of panditas:

1040their descendants became kulinas among the Varendras,
while Aniruddha's descendants remained without kula.

1041Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall tell of the Radhis.

1042Vidyasagara, Bhavadeva and Damodara,
Parashara and Gunarnava, the best of panditas —

1043having made the division, they joined the Radhis,
[but] their descendants did not become kulinas.

1044Bhavadeva Bhatta established the ten samskaras —
[his work] is called the Dasha-karma-paddhati114.

1045After the division into Radhis and Varendras
twenty panditas entered Ballala's assembly.

1046Of the Shandilyas: Shakuni Mishra, whom some call Sugana,
Mahadeva and Vaidyanatha Mahashaya,

1047the great pandita Dharmamshu, whom some call Dharmanga.
I shall tell of the panditas of the Kashyapa gotra:

1048Srikara Adhvaryu, Srikantha Acharya,
Hiranya Acharya and Laulika Acharya.

1049Of the Vatsyas: Pingala Bhatta and Varaha Bhatta,
and also Hingula Mishra, whom some call Nishapati.

1050Of the Bharadvaja gotra, a mighty pandita:
Kolai Sannyasi, his other name Kolahala.

1051Of the Savarnas: Havi Brahmachari and Kulapati,
two brothers, great panditas, [like] Brihaspati in intellect.

1052Their descendants became kulinas among the Radhis.
Dharai Upadhyaya had neither sons nor daughters.

1053Of the Vatsyas: Dhana and Shukra, two foremost panditas,
greatly learned in the Vedas, Vedanta and other shastras.

1054Of the Bharadvajas: Gunakara and Lakshmana, two,
on whose lips all the Vedas always dwell.

1055Of the Savarnas: Govinda and Narayana, two,
supreme panditas, as all know.

1056Their descendants in Rarh and Varendra
did not become kulinas — all know this.

1057These are Ballala's twenty court panditas;
together with the former eleven they are thirty-one.

1058Formerly there were marriages between Radhis and Varendras;
after kulinism was established, this ceased.

1059Dharai Upadhyaya, the best pandita of Ballala's assembly,
wrote the genealogies of the Kanaujis under the name Kula-sagara115.

1060From Adishura to Ballala's [institution of] kulinism —
the genealogies of eleven hundred brahmanas are recorded in it.

1061The descendants of the five rishis numbered eleven hundred [families];
the names Radhi and Varendra became established for them.

1062Narayana, Sushena, Dharadhara, Gautama, Parashara —
their descendants became the best in the Varendra kula.

1063Narayana, Daksha, Chhandada, Sriharsha, Vedagarbha —
their descendants became the whole wealth of the Radhi kula.

1064Narayana's descendants went into both kulas,
and in both kulas they obtained kulinism.

1065Some became kulinas, some became shrotriyas,
and many remained without kula, respected by no one.

1066Why this happened, O hearers —
all these matters I shall describe.

1067The king, seeing the learning and brahmanical worth of the Radhi and Varendra brahmanas, decided in his mind whom he would make kulinas.

1068Concealing this, he devised a stratagem:
"After testing, I shall enhance their dignity."

1069One day, holding an assembly, Maharaja Ballala
without delay says to all the brahmanas:

1070"O brahmanas, hear my words:
I shall establish dignity according to qualities."

1071He carefully fixed an auspicious day
and told all the brahmanas to come to the assembly:

1072"On this auspicious day, before one and a half praharas116,
let all the brahmanas come and assemble.

1073Quickly finishing your daily rites (ahnika) and the rest,
come and appear before one and a half praharas.

1074Whoever comes late
will receive little dignity."

1075Saying this, Ballala dismissed the assembly.
The appointed day arrived.

1076Hastily finishing their ahnika and the rest,
many brahmanas came within one and a half praharas.

1077Some brahmanas came after two praharas —
to them he showed great honour.

1078Some brahmanas came after two and a half praharas —
Ballala honoured them greatly.

1079Ballala says: "The daily and occasional duties of a brahmana
can never be done before one and a half praharas.

1080In two praharas the work is finished with difficulty,
in two and a half it is properly accomplished.

1081Those who came after two and a half praharas
are by the shastras endowed with nine qualities;

1082those who came after two praharas
are by the shastras endowed with eight qualities;

1083those who came at one and a half praharas
are by the shastras endowed with few qualities."

1084Those who came after two and a half praharas,
seeing [in them] nine qualities, he made kulinas117;

1085those who came after two praharas,
seeing eight qualities, he counted as shuddha-shrotriyas;

1086those who came at one and a half praharas,
seeing few qualities, he counted as kashta-shrotriyas.

1087Kulinas and shrotriyas are the chief among brahmanas;
other brahmanas, non-kulinas, are counted as secondary.

1088The test at that time was no test:
it was only a stratagem of Ballala Sena.

1089Which brahmanas were best in learning and brahmanical worth
he had determined beforehand.

1090It was the pious knowers of the Vedas whom he made kulinas and shrotriyas,
and the impious brahmanas whom he counted as kashta-shrotriyas.

1091All the impious brahmanas devoid of learning and brahmanical worth —
they were the ones who came at one and a half praharas.

1092Hoping to receive honour, they came quickly:
they could not understand Ballala's intention.

1093Ballala recognised them as impious
and counted them as kashta-shrotriyas, secondary non-kulinas.

1094All those secondary non-kulinas, bad shrotriyas,
in Rarh and Varendra became kashta-shrotriyas.

1095Marriages were contracted between kulinas and shuddha-shrotriyas;
later this rule disappeared.

1096What rule was established after Ballala —
listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind.

1097Marriages were contracted between kulina and kulina;
kulinas did not give their daughters to others.

1098A kulina takes [in marriage] a shrotriya's daughter,
and in this the dignity of the kulina's kula remains.

1099The shrotriyas, giving a daughter to a kulina,
obtained honour in society.

1100If a kulina gives a daughter to a shrotriya,
the honour of his kula will certainly decrease.

1101All the secondary non-kulinas, the kashta-shrotriyas,
are outcastes (apankteya) in kulina society:

1102kulinas do not marry their daughters;
know for certain: if one marries, the kula perishes.

1103Saying that the kula perishes, kulina brahmanas,
in the name of the kula, do not touch them.

1104But if shuddha-shrotriyas marry
the daughters of kashta-shrotriyas, their kula does not perish.

1105This rule was established after Ballala
and gradually became lax.

1106Udayana Acharya Bhaduri and the ghataka Devivara
again reformed [the families of] the Radhis and Varendras.

1107Udayana first reformed the Varendra kula,
he whom all call a famous naiyayika (logician).

1108A long time after him the ghataka Devivara [of the] Bandya [family]
reformed the Radhi kula in detail118.

1109Hear of the dispute of the Radhis and Varendras:
each call their own ancestors the performers of the sacrifice.

1110Narayana, Sushena-muni and Dharadhara,
and the foremost panditas Gautama and Parashara —

1111these five the genealogists of the Varendras
call the performers of Adishura's sacrifice.

1112Narayana, Daksha-muni and Chhandada,
Sriharsha and Vedagarbha, the best of panditas —

1113these five the ghatakas of the Radhis
call the performers of Adishura's sacrifice.

1114The Varendras say the Radhis came later;
the Radhis say the Varendras joined later.

1115Over this there is constant dispute.
Now I shall tell of the kulinism of the Radhis and Varendras.

1116The Radhis have eight gains (family designations) of kulinas, the Varendras eight;
pay attention to this, O hearers.

1117Of the Shandilyas, Bandyaghati; of the Kashyapas, Chatuti;
of the Vatsyas, Putitunda, Ghoshal, Kanjilal;

1118of the Savarnas, Ganguli and Kundagain;
of the Bharadvajas, the gain Mukhuti — know this for certain.

1119Among the Varendras in the Shandilya gotra, Bagchi and Lahiri:
one [gain] Bagchi [divided] in two, named Rudra and Sadhu.

1120Of the Kashyapas, the gain Maitra and Bhaduri:
Ballala made them kulinas, and their honour became great.

1121Of the Vatsyas, the gain Sanjamini, whom they call Sanyal,
and also the gain Bhima Kaliyai — know this for certain.

1122Of the Bharadvajas the kulinas are the Bhadada-gramis;
of the Savarnas no one obtained kulinism.

1123Of the Kashyapas, the kulinas of the gain Chatta are five:
Bahurupa, Sucha, Aravinda, Halayudha, Bangal.

1124Of the Shandilyas, [the kulinas] Bandyaghati are Maheshvara, Jahlana,
Devala, Makaranda, Ishana, Vamana.

1125Of the Bharadvajas, [the kulinas] Mukhuti are Utsaha and Garudai;
of the Savarnas, Shishu Ganguli and Roshakara Kundagain.

1126Of the Vatsyas, Kanu and Kutuhala Kanjilal,
Govardhana Putitunda and Shiro Ghoshal.

1127Thus I have named the kulinas of the Radhis;
now I shall name the kulinas of the Varendras.

1128Of the Shandilyas, Sadhu Bagchi and Rudra Bagchi,
and the very wise Lokanatha Lahiri.

1129Of the Kashyapas, Kratu Bhaduri and Matu Maitra, two,
honoured by Ballala, the best of kulinas.

1130Of the Vatsyas, Lakshmidhara [of the] gain Sanjamini, or Sanyal,
Jayamala Mishra [of the] gain Bhima Kaliyai.

1131In the Bharadvaja gotra the kulina is Veda Bhadada;
[all] of the Savarna gotra remained without kula.

1132Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall recount the genealogies of the kulinas119.

1133Kshitisha of the Shandilya gotra is foremost among panditas;
his son is Bhatta Narayana, some call him Narayana Bhatta.

1134His son is Adivaraha, his son Vainateya,
his son Subuddhi, his son Vibudheya.

1135His son is Gau, some call him Gui;
Vibudheya's other son is Subhiksha Mahashaya.

1136Gui's sons are Gangadhara and Hakucha;
Gangadhara's son is Suhasa, some call him Pahasa.

1137Suhasa's son was named Shakuni;
some ghatakas call him Sugana.

1138Shakuni's two sons, Jahlana and Maheshvara,
became the best kulinas in the Bandya family.

1139Gui's other son is Hakucha Mahashaya;
his son is Jitamitra, as all know.

1140His son is Svami, his son Vaidyanatha;
Vaidya's son, Ishana Bandya, obtained kulinism.

1141Vibudheya's other son is Subhiksha Mahashaya;
his two sons are Aniruddha and Bhayapaha.

1142Aniruddha's son is called Pithai, some say Piyai;
his son is Dharmamshu, some call him Dharmanga.

1143His sons are Devala and Vamana Bandyaghati;
in Ballala's assembly they obtained kulinism.

1144Subhiksha's other son is Bhayapaha;
his son is Dharana, some call him Dharani.

1145His son is Mahadeva, his son Makaranda Bandya;
obtaining kulinism, he became honoured among brahmanas.

1146Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall recount the various opinions of various ghatakas.

1147Some say: Gangadhara's son is Suhasa,
his sons are Shakuni and Budhaka.

1148Shakuni's sons, Maheshvara and Jahlana,
became the chief kulinas in the Bandya family.

1149Shakuni's other son is Budhaka Mahashaya;
his sons are Mahadeva, Vaidyanatha, Dharmanga.

1150Mahadeva's son was named Makaranda,
Vaidyanatha's son is Ishana Bandya.

1151Dharmanga's sons are Devala and Vamana,
the chief kulinas in the Bandyaghati family.

1152Hear, all of you, the opinion of other ghatakas:
Narayana Bhatta's son is Adivaraha,

1153Adivaraha's son is Vainateya,
his son's name is Vibudheya,

1154his sons are Gau and Subhiksha Mahashaya;
Gau's son is Hakucha, his son Svami,

1155his son is Vaidyanatha Mahashaya,
and his son is the kulina Ishana Bandya.

1156Vitaraga of the Kashyapa gotra is foremost among panditas;
his son is the very wise Daksha-muni.

1157Daksha's son was named Sulochana;
his sons are Mahadeva and Vasudeva.

1158Mahadeva's son is Haladhara; his sons are Krishnadeva,
another son Narideva, and also Rupadeva.

1159Krishnadeva's son is Varaha Mahashaya;
his son is Srikara Adhvaryu.

1160His son Bahurupa became a kulina —
the foremost in the Chatuti family.

1161Haladhara's other son is Narideva;
his son's name is Lalo Mahashaya.

1162Lalo's sons are Garudadhvaja and Bharata;
some call Bharata Samanta.

1163Garudadhvaja's sons are Srikantha and Hiranya;
Srikantha's son, Bangal Chatta, obtained kulinism.

1164Hiranya's son is Halayudha Chatta;
honoured by Ballala, he obtained kulinism.

1165Lalo's other son is Bharata, whom they call Samanta;
his son is Laulika Acharya Mahashaya.

1166His sons are Sucha and Aravinda Chatta;
in Ballala's assembly their kulinism was manifested.

1167Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear the various opinions of various ghatakas.

1168Some say: he who was Haladhara's son is Rupadeva,
and they consider Garudadhvaja and Bharata his sons.

1169Garuda's sons are Srikantha and Hiranya;
Srikantha's son is Bangal, Hiranya's son they call Halayudha.

1170Bharata's son is Laulika Mahashaya,
his sons are Sucha and Aravinda Chatta.

1171Others say: Daksha's son is Sulochana,
his son Vasudeva, his son they call Vishvambhara;

1172his sons are Narideva and Rupadeva,
another son's name is Mahadeva.

1173Narideva's son is Varaha Mahashaya,
his son is Srikara Adhvaryu,

1174his sons are Bahurupa and Halayudha Chatta:
in Ballala's assembly their kulinism was manifested.

1175Vishvambhara's other son was named Rupadeva;
his son is Garuda, abode of all virtues,

1176his son is Srikantha Acharya, a good pandita;
his son, the excellent pandita Bangal, obtained kulinism.

1177Vishvambhara's further son is Mahadeva;
his son is Siya, his son is called Chahala.

1178Chahala's son is Laulika Acharya Mahashaya;
his sons are Aravinda and Sucha Chatta.

1179Sudhanidhi of the Vatsya gotra is a great sage;
his son's name is the great muni Chhandada.

1180He had many sons, foremost among panditas;
listen attentively to what I shall now tell.

1181Chhandada's son is Surabhi, his son Pingala,
his son Shiro Ghoshal became a kulina.

1182Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear the various opinions of various ghatakas.

1183Some say: Surabhi's son is Sagara Mahashaya,
his son Manoratha, his son Vishvamitra,

1184his son Jitamitra, his son Bhagavan,
his son Pingala Bhatta, foremost among panditas.

1185Pingala's son was named Shiro Ghoshal;
honouring him, Ballala conferred kulinism on him.

1186Chhandada's other son is Sridhara Mahashaya;
his son was named Vedagarbha.

1187His son's name is Vasundhara,
his son is Hingula Bhatta Mahashaya,

1188his sons are Kanu and Kutuhala Kanjilal;
honouring them, Ballala conferred kulinism on them.

1189Sridhara's family the various ghatakas describe variously;
I shall tell the hearers what it is.

1190Some say: Sridhara's son is Yajneshvara;
some call him Vedagarbha, others Hemagarbha;

1191his son is Nishapati, another name Hingula;
his sons are Kanjilal, Kanu and Kutuhala.

1192Others say: Sridhara's son is Yajneshvara,
some call him Vedagarbha;

1193his son is Hemagarbha, his son Vasundhara,
his son Praneshvara, his son Gunakara,

1194his son Nishapati, some call him Hingula;
his sons are Kanjilal, Kanu and Kutuhala.

1195Some call Kanjilal Kanjibilli:
Kanjibilli and Kanjilal mean the same.

1196Others say: Sridhara's son is Yajneshvara,
his son Hemagarbha, his son Vasundhara,

1197his son Praneshvara, his son Guna;
Guna's son was named Nishapati;

1198Nishapati's son was named Hingula Pandita,
his sons are Kanjilal, Kanu and Kutuhala.

1199Still others say: Praneshvara's son is Gunakara,
his sons are Hingula and Varaha;

1200Hingula's son is Kutuhala Kanjilal,
Varaha's son is Kanu Kanjilal.

1201Chhandada's son is Vira; some say Dhira,
some firmly call him Ravi.

1202His son is Jaimini, another name Lakshmidhara;
his son is Utsaha, other names Basala and Nilambara.

1203His son is Govardhana Acharya Putitunda:
obtaining kulinism, he became the best of brahmanas.

1204O hearers, various ghatakas have various opinions;
disclosing them, I shall describe them.

1205Some say: Chhandada's son is Ravi, whom they call Dhira;
a son named Jaimini was born to him;

1206his son is Lakshmidhara, his son Bala,
his son's name was Amshula;

1207Amshula's son was named Vallabha Mahashaya,
his son Nilambara, another name Utsaha;

1208his son is Govardhana Acharya Putitunda:
obtaining kulinism, he became the best of brahmanas.

1209[Others say:] Chhandada's son is Ravi, some call him Vira;
a son named Jaimini was born to him;

1210his son is Tamopaha, his son Vanamali,
his son Vatsala, his son Dhiravani,

1211his son Utsaha Acharya Mahashaya,
his son Govardhana Puti[tunda].

1212[Others:] Dhira's son is Jaimini, his son Tamopaha,
his son Lakshmidhara, his son they call Vanamali,

1213his son Vatsala, his son Ramana,
his son Utsaha, his son Puti Govardhana.

1214The son of Medhatithi of the Bharadvaja gotra is Sriharsha;
his son is Srigarbha, as all know.

1215His son was named Srinivasa;
a son named Arava was born to him.

1216His son is Trivikrama, foremost among panditas,
his son the very wise Kaka Mishra.

1217His son was named Sadhu, some say Dhadhu;
his son is Jalashaya, righteous in all deeds.

1218His son is Suresha, some call him Baneshvara;
his son is Guha, whom they call Gui.

1219His son is Madhava Acharya Mahashaya;
his son is Kulai Sannyasi, some call him Kolahala.

1220His sons are Utsaha and Garuda Mukhuti;
in Ballala's assembly they worthily obtained kulinism.

1221O hearers, hear the various opinions of various ghatakas:
disclosing them, I shall describe them.

1222Some say: Sriharsha's son is Dhadhu,
his son Gui, his son they call Gadaka,

1223his son Shubhana, his son Madhava Acharya,
his son Kolahala, excellent in every respect,

1224his sons Utsaha and Garuda Mukhuti:
in Ballala's assembly they worthily obtained kulinism.

1225Saubhari of the Savarna gotra is a great muni;
his son is Vedagarbha, a great sage.

1226His sons are Madana and the noble Haladhara;
Hala's other name is Viravrata Kulapati.

1227Madana's son was named Ratnagarbha;
a son named Visha was born to him.

1228Visha's son was named Heramba;
his son Mangala, some call him Manguli;

1229his son Hari Brahmachari Mahashaya,
his son Roshakara Kundagain.

1230Vedagarbha's other son is Viravrata Kulapati;
his son Shubhana, his son the noble Gauri,

1231his son Pitambara, his son Damodara,
his son Kulapati, his other name Kuloka (?).

1232Kulapati's son was named Shishu Ganguli;
in Ballala's assembly he joyfully obtained kulinism.

1233Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear the various opinions of various ghatakas.

1234Some say: Hala, whom they call Viravrata,
had a son named Hemagarbha;

1235his son Padmagarbha, his son Kushali,
his son Shobhana, his son Gauri.

1236Gaurikanta's son is Udhaka (?) Mahashaya,
his son named Kulapati;

1237his son was named Shishu Ganguli:
in Ballala's assembly he joyfully obtained kulinism.

1238I have described the genealogies of the Radhi kulinas;
hear the genealogies of the Varendra kulinas.

1239Kshitisha of the Shandilya gotra is the best of panditas;
his son is Narayana, endowed with all virtues.

1240Narayana Bhatta some call Bhatta Narayana;
his son is Adigai Ojha.

1241His son is Jayamani Bhatta, some call him Jayamana;
his son is Hari […], another name Harikrishna.

1242His son is Vidyapati, foremost among panditas,
his son the very wise Raghupati.

1243His son was named Shivacharya;
Shivacharya's son was named Somacharya.

1244His son is Ugramani, the best of panditas,
his son Tapomani, a keen-minded pandita.

1245His son was named Sindhusagara,
his son was named Bindusagara.

1246Bindusagara's two sons are Jayasagara and Manisagara:
Jaya [remained] in Varendra, Mani went to Rarh —
the genealogists call him a Radhi.

1247Jayasagara's sons are keen-minded panditas:
Madhava, Mauna Bhatta, Svarnarekha, Pitambara.

1248Madhava [received the village] Champati, Mauna Bhatta Nandana:
"Nandana," "resident of Nandana," "Nandami" mean the same.

1249They became shrotriyas in Ballala's assembly;
Svarnarekha, becoming a shrotriya, received the village of Sihari.

1250Some call Svarnarekha Svarnadeva;
know this for certain, O hearers.

1251Jayasagara's other son is Pitambara, foremost among panditas;
three very learned sons were born to him:

1252Sadhu Bagchi, Rudra Bagchi and Lokanatha Lahiri —
honoured by Ballala, they became eminent kulinas.

1253Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear the various opinions of various genealogists.

1254Some say: Narayana's son is Adigai Ojha,
his son the mighty Jayamani Bhatta,

1255his sons are foremost among panditas,
[among them] the very learned Harikrishna Mishra;

1256Hari's son is Shivacharya, his son Somacharya,
[his son] Ugramani, the best of panditas,

1257his son Tapomani, his son Sindhusagara,
his son Bindusagara, the best of panditas,

1258his sons Jayasagara and Manisagara;
Manisagara's other name is Vidyasagara;
Jayasagara [remained] in Varendra, Mani went to the Radhis.

1259Others say: Adi[gai]'s son is Jayamani Bhatta,
his son Harikrishna, his son they call Shivacharya,

1260his son Somacharya, his son Ugramani,
Ugramani's son was named Tapomani,

1261his son Sindhusagara, a keen-minded pandita,
his sons Jayasagara and Vidyasagara:

1262Jaya [remained] a Varendra, Vidyasagara went to the Radhis;
among genealogists his other name is Manisagara.

1263Still others say: Adi[gai]'s son is Jayamana,
he has a son named Harikrishna,

1264his son Shivacharya, foremost among panditas,
his son the very wise Somacharya,

1265his son Ugramani, the best of panditas,
his son Tapomani, a keen-minded pandita,

1266his son Vidyapati Mahashaya,
he has a son named Raghupati,

1267Raghu's sons are Sindhusagara and Bindusagara;
Sindhu's son is Jayasagara, Bindu's son Vidyasagara;

1268Vidyasagara's other name is Manisagara,
a supreme pandita, the abode of all virtues.

1269Vitaraga of the Kashyapa gotra is foremost among panditas;
his son is Sushena-muni, endowed with great virtues,

1270his son Brahma Ojha, his son Daksha,
his son Shantanu, a pandita, master of all the shastras,

1271his son was named Pitambara Pandita,
his son Hiranyagarbha, renowned in the world.

1272Some say: Daksha's son is Pitambara Pandita,
his son Shantanu, his son Hiranya Pandita.

1273Hiranya's son is Bhugarbha (?), his son Vedagarbha;
Veda's son is Jigani, Mahamuni, some call him Jaganmuni;

1274some call him Jaganmahamuni.
Jigani is childless; Mahamuni has two sons:

1275two panditas, Svarnarekha and Bhavadeva Bhatta;
Svarnarekha [remained] a Varendra, Bhavadeva went to the Radhis.

1276Svarnarekha's son is Sindhu, some call him Sandhyaika Ojha;
his son is the very wise Garuda.

1277Garuda's sons are Kratu Bhaduri and Matu Maitra;
honoured by Ballala, they obtained kulinism.

1278Kratu is called Kaitai, Matu Maitai;
some call [them] Kaitai Bhaduri and Maitai Maitra.

1279Sudhanidhi of the Vatsya gotra is very wise;
his son's name is Dharadhara-muni,

1280his son Veda Ojha Mahashaya,
his son Siddheshvara Pathaka, some call him Sidhu,

1281his son Chaturbhuja Chaturvedacharya;
some say his other name is Chaturvedantacharya.

1282Siddheshvara's other son is Damodara Ojha;
Chaturbhuja Chaturveda [remained] with the Varendras, Damodara went to the Radhis.

1283Some say: Veda Ojha's son is Nabhika (?) Acharya,
his son Shulapani, the best of panditas,

1284his son Lakhai, his son Hiru (?),
his son's name is Kalpataru,

1285his son Mantu (?), his son Sidhu,
a supreme pandita, righteous in all deeds,

1286his son Chaturbhuja Chaturvedacharya,
another son's name is the excellent Damodara Shukla (?).

1287Chaturvedacharya remained in the Varendra kula,
and Damodara Ojha went and joined the Radhis.

1288Damodara's sons are Dhana and Shukra Mahashaya:
Dhana goes to Varendra, Shukra stays in Rarh.

1289Chaturbhuja Chaturveda has many sons;
now I shall recount their names.

1290Harihara Kad-muriyal (?) Mahashaya,
honoured by Ballala, obtained shrotriya status.

1291Lakshmidhara Sanjamini, or Sanyal —
honouring him, Ballala conferred kulinism on him.

1292Jayamana Mishra [of the] gain Bhima-Kaliyai,
honoured by Ballala, obtained kulinism.

1293Shaktidhara [became] a shrotriya [with the] gain Taluri,
Shashadhara a shrotriya [with the gain] Kamadeva-Kaliyai.

1294Divakara Acharya is foremost among panditas;
to him Ballala granted the village of Bhadiyal.

1295Honoured by Ballala, they received honour.
Listen attentively to what I shall now tell.

1296Medhatithi of the Bharadvaja gotra is very wise;
his son is the excellent pandita, the great muni Gautama.

1297His son was named Vibhakara,
his son they call Prabhakara.

1298His son is Vishnu Mishra, foremost among panditas,
his son Kakutstha, another name Kaku.

1299Kakutstha has two sons, foremost among panditas:
Gopinatha Ojha and Prajapati Agnihotrika.

1300Gopinatha's son is Vachaspati Mahashaya,
another name Gunakara, the abode of all virtues,

1301his son Akashavasi, whom they call Akai,
his son Narayana Panchatapa.

1302Narayana's son is Vardhamana Agnihotrika,
a supreme pandita, a treasury of all virtues,

1303his son Prithvidhara, an excellent pandita,
his son's name is Sharabha Acharya.

1304Sharabha's other name is Marara;
his son is Matanga, whom they call Matta Ojha,

1305his son Jihmani, also Jaimini Acharya,
a supreme pandita, excellent in all virtues,

1306his sons Bhaskara the Vedantist and Parashara Ojha:
Bhaskara [remained] a Varendra, the mighty Parashara went to Rarh.

1307Bhaskara's sons are Kana, Dhana, Sukashi, Bhuvana,
Vinayaka, and another son, Sayana Acharya.

1308Kana [received] the village of Gochchhasi, Dhana Gogram,
Sukashi Gosvalambi, Bhuvana the village of Aturthi;

1309Vinayaka received the village of Uchchharika,
its other name is Uchchhakudhi.

1310All of them are foremost among panditas;
honoured by Ballala, they obtained shrotriya status.

1311Sayanacharya's sons are Ada, Aru, Atu Ojha,
very mighty, excellent panditas, masters of the Vedas.

1312Ada, honoured by Ballala, took the village of Bampati;
Bampati's other name is Jhamal.

1313Aru, becoming a shrotriya, received the village of Nadli:
Nadli, Nadiyal, Naudi mean the same.

1314Atu Ojha, becoming a shrotriya, took Ratnavali;
some call him Annu Acharya.

1315Honoured by Ballala, they are most excellent panditas;
in the family of Aru Advaita Prabhu was born120.

1316Sayana's other son is Vedacharya Mahashaya;
honouring him, Ballala made him a kulina,

1317granting him the village of Bhadada, he did him honour:
in the family of Gautama Veda Bhadada became chief.

1318When Udayana Bhaduri appeared,
at that time the kulinism of the Bhadada family [was lost]:

1319through association with Udayana's son their kula perished,
and Udayana calls the Bhadadas "fillers of the row" (pankti-puraka).

1320Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall describe another branch of Gautama.

1321Gautama's fifth descendant is Kakutstha;
his son is Prajapati Agnihotrika,

1322his son Gopinatha Ojha Mahashaya,
his son Siddheshvara Vachaspati.

1323Vachaspati's sons are Gunakara and the noble Lakshmana:
Gunakara lives in Varendra, Lakshmana in Rarh.

1324A certain genealogist describes Gautama's family differently;
I shall tell the hearers what it is.

1325Gautama's son is Vibhakara, his son Prabhakara,
his son Vishnu Mishra, the best of panditas,

1326his son was named Kakutstha Mahashaya,
his son Prajapati Agnihotrika,

1327his son was named Matanga Ojha,
his son the mighty Jaimini Acharya,

1328his sons Bhaskara the Vedantist and Parashara:
Bhaskara [remained] in Varendra, Parashara went to the Radhis.

1329Saubhari of the Savarna gotra is a mahashaya;
his son is Parashara-muni.

1330Parashara has two sons, foremost among panditas,
named Mahipati and Digambara Ojha.

1331Mahipati's son was named Pashupati,
a supreme pandita, [like] Brihaspati in intellect;

1332he has a son named Kulapati,
his son is Narayana Agnihotrika,

1333Narayana's son is Divakara Ojha,
his son the mighty Somacharya,

1334his sons Aniruddha and Gunarnava:
Aniruddha [remained] in Varendra, Gunarnava went to the Radhis.

1335Parashara's other son is Digambara Ojha;
his son is the mighty Aniruddha,

1336his son was named Lambodara,
he has a son named Makaradhvaja,

1337his son Madhava Acharya Mahashaya,
he has a son named Bharata Pathaka,

1338his son was named Vidyananda,
Vidyananda's son was named Bhavananda,

1339Bhavananda's sons are Govinda and Narayana:
Govinda [remained] a Varendra, Narayana went to Rarh.

1340Hear the various opinions of various genealogists;
disclosing them, I shall describe them.

1341Some say: Parashara's son is Divakara,
some call him Digambara;

1342Divakara's son is Aniruddha Mahashaya,
his son Sudhakara, his son Vishvambhara,

1343his son Lambodara, his son Durgavara,
his son Makaradhvaja, the best of panditas,

1344Makara's sons Madhava Acharya and Gopala Acharya,
Madhava's son Bharata Pathaka Mahashaya,

1345Bharata's sons Vidyananda and Bhavananda,
Vidyananda's sons Bhavanicharana, Shubhananda,

1346Viprananda, Mukunda, Devi-nandana —
all of them most excellent panditas;

1347Bhavananda's sons Govinda and Narayana:
Govinda [remained] a Varendra, Narayana went to Rarh.

1348Having studied the Kula-ratna and other books,
I have described the genealogies of the kulinas.

1349The divergent opinions I heard from the mouths of the kulacharyas
I have all written down, noting that they are differing opinions.

1350Among the kulacharyas there is no unity of opinion;
which is true and which false, [only] the Gosani knows121.

1351Among the Radhis there are eight [gains of] siddha-shrotriyas:
of the Shandilyas, Batavyal, Mashachataka, Kushari,

1352of the Kashyapas, Pakrashi, whom they call Parkati,
Paldhi and Shimlai, know this for certain,

1353of the Vatsyas, Shimlal and the gain Kanjari;
among the Bharadvajas and Savarnas there are no siddha-shrotriyas.

1354Among the Varendras there are eight [gains of] siddha-shrotriyas:
of the Shandilyas, Champati and Nandanavasi,

1355of the Kashyapas the siddha-shrotriyas are the gain Karanja,
of the Vatsyas, Bhattashali and Kamadeva Kaliyai —

1356Kamakali is called Kamadeva Kaliyai;
know this for certain, O hearers —

1357of the Bharadvajas, Nadli, whom they call Nadiyal,
and the gain Jhampati, whom they call Jhamal,

1358and the gain Atartha, whom they call Aturthi;
among the Savarnas there are no siddha-shrotriyas at all.

1359Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall tell of the sadhya-shrotriyas of the Radhis.

1360Of the Shandilyas: Kusuma, Seyaka, Akasha, Ghoshali,
Basuyani, Karala and Kulakuli;

1361of the Kashyapas: Amudi (?), Tailabati, Bhurishtal,
Pushali, Palashai, Koyari, Bhatta, Mula;

1362of the Vatsyas the sadhya is the gain Bapuli;
of the Bharadvajas the gain Sani (?), know this for certain;

1363of the Savarnas: Pumsika, Nandi, Siyari and Sat,
Dayi, Nai, Pari, Bali, Siddhal — [these are] made known.

1364Of the Shandilyas seven, of the Kashyapas eight,
of the Vatsyas one, of the Bharadvajas one, of the Savarnas nine.

1365Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall describe the sadhya-shrotriyas of the Varendras.

1366Of the Shandilyas: Sihari and Vishakha, whom they call Vishi;
of the Kashyapas: Madhugrami, whom they also call Modhagrami;

1367of the Vatsyas: Kurmuriyal, known by the name Kurumba,
Yanarudhi (?), Bhadiyal and the gain Kaliyai;

1368of the Bharadvajas: the gain Rai and Ratnavali,
the gain Udrukhi (?), whom they call Uchchharukhi,

1369the gain Gosvalambi, whom they call Goshalakshi,
and others call Goshrigal and Gopurvarvi;

1370the people of Gochhariyal some call Gochatti,
others know them as Gochchhas;

1371the gain Kharjuri, whom they also call Khorjar,
and also the gain Sariyal, know for certain.

1372In the Savarna gotra there are no sadhya-shrotriyas;
believe this, O hearers.

1373Of the Shandilyas two, of the Kashyapas one, of the Vatsyas four,
of the Bharadvajas seven, of the Savarnas none.

1374Hear, O hearers, of the kashta-shrotriyas of the Radhi class:
they are "enemies of the kula," counted as secondary kulinas.

1375If [a kulina] marries their daughter, the kulina's kula perishes;
that is why they are called enemies of the kula.

1376The kashta-shrotriyas, enemies of the kula, are rejected by kulinas;
I tell their names — accept them all, O hearers.

1377Of the Shandilyas: Dirghangi, Pariha, Kulabhi,
Garagari, Keshari, know this for certain;

1378of the Kashyapas: the gains Podari, Had, Gud, Pitamundi;
of the Vatsyas: the gain Mahinta and Pippalai,

1379Dighali, Chautkhandi and the gain Purva;
of the Bharadvajas: Rai and Dindi, whom they call Dingsai;

1380in the Savarna gotra: Ghantagrami,
some call them Ghanteshvari.

1381Of the Shandilyas five, of the Kashyapas four, of the Vatsyas [five],
of the Bharadvajas two, of the Savarnas one.

1382Hear of the kashta-shrotriyas of the Varendra class:
calling them enemies of the kula, they are counted as secondary.

1383If [a kulina] marries their daughter, the kulina's kula perishes;
that is why they are rejected by kulinas.

1384[Of the Shandilyas:] Matsyashi (?), Todaka, whom they call Totaka,
and some call Suvarna-totaka;

1385the village of Beladi and the village of Bilva —
Bilva some call Champabilva, others Chatubilva;

1386Betagram some call Kalindibeta, others Kamendrabeta,
Thukhuri some call Purana-thukhuri;

1387there is also a very well-known gain named Tadoyal —
so many [gains] are in the Shandilya gotra.

1388Of the Kashyapas the kashta-shrotriyas are the gain Suvi (?),
some call them Sharagram, others Sarvagrami;

1389Balayashtika, Mauhali, whom some call Mauyali;
Balihari some call Balihari;

1390Kirali some call Kirala,
Vishotkata some call Katagrami;

1391there are also the people of Ashrakota (?);
Parisvami some call Paresha, others Sahagram;

1392Mathagram, Madhyagram and Gangagram,
Panchana (?), Bijakunda and Belagram, know;

1393the gain Atharvija is very well known —
some call it Chama-atharvija.

1394I have enumerated the kashta-shrotriyas of the Kashyapas;
O hearers, hear of the kashta-shrotriyas of the Vatsyas:

1395Shitali some call Simuli —
Shitali and Simuli are names of one village;

1396Tanudi some call Taluri,
Devali some call Deuli;

1397Vatsa (?), Kukkati and Shrutavati,
the gain Nidrala and also Akshagramati;

1398Paundra-vardhani some call Paundrikakshi,
some know them as Paundra-kali;

1399Ghoshagram some call Chakshusha-gram,
some know it as Lakshagram;

1400the village of Nagasura some call Sahari,
the village of Tantrakeli they call Kalindi;

1401the village of Shivatati they call Chaturanandi,
the village of Vaishali they know as Dhosali;

1402the village of Boda and the village of Kalihaya.
Now I shall name the kashta-shrotriyas of the Bharadvajas:

1403there are the people of Gogram and the people of Kachudi —
Kachudi some also call Kachchhati;

1404the village of Nanda some call Nani-gram;
the people of Kshetra, or Kritra, and also of the villages Puti and Pippali;

1405the people of Shulagram some call people of Sharangigram,
the people of Shimbibohal they call Shimbibohal;

1406the people of Dadhiyal are very well known;
Nighata some call Nikhata;

1407Balotkata some call Balotkata,
the village of Kunja some call Shakati-kunja, others Kanchana-[kunja];

1408Bhogrami some call Samudra-bhogram.
Now I shall tell of the Savarna gotra:

1409the village of Siudiyar, and also Dadhi and Pakadi —
Pakadi some call Pipadi;

1410the people of Utadi some call Unduri,
the people of Dhukadi some call Dhunduri;

1411there is the village of Mehudi and the village of Nedhudi,
they also name Shringi, Samudra and Naigram;

1412the village of Tuturi and the village of Panchavati,
very well known is the village of Khandavati;

1413the village of Bad some call Tadayar,
the village of Alalta (?) some call Bashe-gram;

1414the village of Shvetaka some call Setuka,
the village of Kalapi some call Kapali;

1415the village of Satili some call Sitali;
Paundra-vardhani some call Ketu-paundra, others Paundra-ketu,

1416some know it as Pundarika;
the people of Nikhata some call Nikhadi.

1417Of the Shandilyas seven, of the Kashyapas fourteen,
of the Vatsyas sixteen, of the Bharadvajas thirteen,

1418of the Savarnas twenty: thus, O hearers,
I have determined the kashta-shrotriyas of the Varendras122.

1419After the passing of Raja Kamsanarayana
Siudiyar and Pakadi among the Savarnas obtained [the rank of] sadhya123.

1420The sadhya-shrotriyas were formerly kashta-shrotriyas;
gradually, by giving daughters to kulinas, they obtained [the rank of] sadhya.

1421Many Radhi and Varendra brahmanas, kashta-shrotriyas,
accept gifts from the unworthy and officiate for those unfit.

1422Some became "varna-brahmanas," others went to other lands
and began to perform rites, worship and recitation [for pay].

1423The magnanimous Ballala, honouring the Radhi and Varendra brahmanas,
divided them into three classes: kulinas, shuddha- and kashta-shrotriyas.

1424According to their dignity he gave names to all;
the brahmanas respect the "Ballala dignity" of the gains.

1425Now I shall tell of the kapas and vamshajas:
hear how and why they arose.

1426Among the Radhis there are vamshajas, among the Varendras kapas;
lend your ears to this, O hearers.

1427In Ballala's assembly those endowed with nine qualities were counted as kulinas,
those endowed with eight qualities received the rank of shuddha-shrotriyas,

1428those endowed with few qualities were counted as kashta-shrotriyas;
some call them secondary kulinas.

1429They are enemies of the kula, counted as non-brahmanas;
in brahmana society they became disrespected.

1430By accepting gifts from the unworthy and officiating for those unfit,
they all became outcastes.

1431Those kulinas who took their daughters [in marriage]
became unfit in society.

1432In Ballala's time the brahmanas were divided into three classes;
later one more, new group arose.

1433A kulina who married a kashta-shrotriya's daughter
remains unfit in society.

1434Those kulinas who give a daughter to a kashta-shrotriya
become outcastes in society.

1435From [unions of] kashta-shrotriyas with kulinas a new family arose;
they were given the name "vamshaja."

1436If a kulina takes a vamshaja's daughter
or gives a daughter to a vamshaja,

1437he becomes unfit in society and receives the name vamshaja.
Thus many vamshajas arose.

1438Ganai, Had, Jhithu — these three Bandyaghatis,
Hasya Ganguli and Shakuni Chatuti —

1439by accepting gifts from the unworthy and officiating for those unfit,
by marrying the daughters of kashta-shrotriyas

1440and giving their daughters to kashta-shrotriyas,
they lost their place in society.

1441Having done this, they became unfit in society,
and a group of kulinas entered among them:

1442Vasishtha took Ganai's daughter,
Thotha married Shakuni's daughter,

1443Dayaka married Had's daughter,
Chakrapani and Kuvera took Hasya's two daughters,

1444Kulabhushana Chatta took Jhithu's daughter —
from these six came the name "vamshaja."

1445Garagari, Pippalai, Dindi or Dingsai,
Mahinta, Pitamundi and the gain Ghanta,

1446Dirghangi, Pariha, Kulabhi, Podari,
Had, Gud, the gain Rai and Keshari,

1447Dighali, Chautkhandi and the gain Purva —
these seventeen gains I count as kashta-shrotriyas.

1448They constantly intermarry with the vamshajas,
and therefore they too received the name vamshaja.

1449Devivara made them kashta-shrotriyas again,
and the kulinas who had become vamshajas remained outcastes.

1450The vamshajas remain engaged in bad deeds:
some became agradanis (receivers of funeral gifts), some joined the varna-brahmanas,

1451some perform rites and worship and serve as cooks,
others go off to other lands.

1452Officiating for shudras, serving as temple priests and cooks,
the kashta-shrotriyas and vamshajas settle in various lands.

1453How Devivara described [the status of] the vamshajas —
listen, O hearers, I shall tell what it is.

1454A kulina who gives a daughter to a shuddha- or sadhya-shrotriya is a vamshaja;
a kulina who gives a daughter to a kashta-shrotriya is a vamshaja;

1455a kulina who takes a vamshaja's daughter is a vamshaja;
a kulina who gives a daughter to a vamshaja is a vamshaja;

1456a kulina with whom kulinas do not intermarry
I count among the vamshajas.

1457[Formerly] a kulina who took a kashta-shrotriya's daughter [became] a vamshaja;
Devivara abolished this rule:

1458one who takes a kashta-shrotriya's daughter loses dignity,
but by giving a daughter to a great kulina he becomes respected again.

1459Marriages used to be contracted between shuddha-shrotriyas and kulinas,
and by this the kulina's kula did not perish;

1460Devivara abolished this rule,
and now Devivara's opinion began to be followed.

1461O hearers, you have heard the account of the vamshajas;
now I shall tell of the kapas among the Varendras.

1462In Ballala's assembly those endowed with nine qualities became kulinas,
those endowed with eight qualities were counted as shuddha-shrotriyas,

1463those endowed with few qualities as kashta-shrotriyas,
whom kulinas and shuddha-shrotriyas always reject.

1464If any kulina took a kashta-shrotriya's daughter,
all reviled him as a "kapa."

1465"Kapa" is explained as "one who obtains the bad" (ku-apnoti):
because he ruins the kula out of greed, he is reviled as a "kapa."

1466The offspring of kulinas by kashta-shrotriya women
were despised under the name kapa.

1467Kashta-shrotriyas, shuddha-shrotriyas, kulinas —
into three classes Ballala divided the brahmanas.

1468A long time afterwards the kapas arose;
I shall tell how the kapas increased.

1469A resident of the village of Vaniati, Udayana Acharya,
composed the Nyaya-kusumanjali and other excellent books124.

1470By his authority the kulinism of the Bhadadas was destroyed:
he declared the Bhadadas "fillers of the row."

1471*"First Maitra, then Bhima, Rudra, Sanjamini, Sadhu,
Lahiri and Bhaduri; and Bhadada — the filler of the row."*125

1472Udayana created the karana and the custom of parivarta;
from his son came the community of kapas.

1473[Formerly,] if a kulina intermarried with a shuddha-shrotriya,
the kulina's kula suffered no harm.

1474Udayana put an end to this rule
and established a new one:

1475"Marriages shall be contracted between kulina and kulina;
kulinas shall no longer give daughters to shrotriyas.

1476Kulinas, by marrying the daughters of kulinas
and of shuddha-shrotriyas, shall make their kula glorious.

1477The karana is made between kulinas,
and the custom of parivarta also remains among kulinas.

1478If there is no daughter, they shall make a girl of kusha grass
and, giving her away, make the kula glorious126.

1479The shrotriya places a mark (phonta) on the forehead of the kulina bridegroom —
in this their karana consists.

1480A shrotriya shall give his daughter to a kulina —
by this the shrotriya's honour increases.

1481Between kapa and kapa there shall be karana —
by this the kapas become honourable.

1482If a kulina gives a daughter to a shrotriya,
his kula will perish, and he will be counted among the shrotriyas.

1483If a kulina makes a karana with a kapa,
his kula will perish, and he will be counted among the kapas.

1484If a kulina gives a daughter to a kapa
or takes a kapa's daughter,

1485his kula will perish, he will become a kapa, unfit in society."
He enforced yet another very harsh rule:

1486"If a kulina sleeps, eats and so on together with a kapa,
the kulina's kula will be broken."

1487Udayana promulgated this rule.
On parivarta and karana I shall speak in detail later.

1488Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall tell of the ruin of the Bhadada kula and of the kapas.

1489Udayana Acharya Bhaduri had two wives;
the elder, even in old age, remained fond of finery.

1490Udayana says: "Dear, what behaviour is this?
You have grown old, and your love of finery has not gone.

1491I see flowers in the knot of your hair, a garland of flowers on your neck —
your behaviour greatly vexes me."

1492The elder wife says: "My lord, as long as you
remain alive, my love of finery will not diminish."

1493Udayana says: "The younger wife is very sedate,
always absorbed in worshipping her chosen Deity;

1494she has no love of finery at all;
I would like to see you like her.

1495If it is otherwise, I shall surely abandon you;
from today, dear, be careful."

1496After some days Udayana Acharya sees
his elder wife still decked out in finery:

1497in the knot of her hair a lovely garland of champaka,
on her neck bel and bakula shine, and bees hum.

1498Udayana Acharya says in anger: "Sinful woman!
You have grown old, and your love of finery has not gone!"

1499Saying this, he abandoned his elder wife;
her six sons remained with her.

1500To his sons, Bhupati, Bhavanipati and the others,
Udayana keeps saying to abandon their mother.

1501The sons say: "Father, this we cannot do;
taking our mother, we shall go to another land."

1502In anger Udayana says: "You sons,
you have lightly transgressed your father's word!

1503For this bad deed you are counted as kapas:
your kula is gone, you have become contemptible."

1504Hearing this, the sons fell at their father's feet;
relenting, the father said:

1505"From today your kulinism is at an end;
I have told you the chief rule of the karana.

1506Those kulinas who associate with you
will also be counted among the kapas."

1507Seeing their father's severity, the sons
separated and formed their own group.

1508Considering themselves kulinas, they began to make karanas,
and many kulinas came and joined them.

1509Ananda Bhadada was the foremost among them;
from that time the Bhadada kula was ruined.

1510Ananda became the helper of Udayana's sons —
that is why the Bhadadas' kulina dignity was lost.

1511He slept and ate together with the kapas;
for this offence the Bhadadas lost their kula.

1512Other kulinas who were with him
all lost their kula like the Bhadadas.

1513All of them together made karanas
and all were counted among the kapas.

1514The kulina community does not eat with them,
and Bhadada laments in his heart.

1515Seeing no way out, Bhadada goes to Udayana —
and the Bhadadas became "fillers of the row" in the kulina community.

1516Udayana ate in one row with Bhadada —
hence the designation of the Bhadadas as "fillers of the row."

1517By Udayana's grace the Bhadadas became admissible in society,
but their kulina dignity was lost and never returned.

1518Udayana Acharya Bhaduri Mahashaya
examines the faults and merits of the kulinas;

1519seeing their faults and merits, he then, forming equal groups,
divides the kulinas into eight parts127.

1520Udayana's younger wife, of very good character,
bore a son named Pashupati;

1521he became a chief kulina like his father,
equal to his father in learning, very wise.

1522Bhupati and the other sons of the elder wife,
having become kapas, are outcastes in the kulina community.

1523Pashupati's son, Ghaghai, was a great pandita; by the "blow" (aghata) [that makes one] a kapa and by the "depression" (avasada) he determined the eight patis.

1524One who is suspected of deeds contrary to society and dharma,
even if he did not commit them —

1525he is punishable by society;
this punishment the genealogists call "aghata" and "avasada":

1526the heavy punishment is aghata, the light one avasada;
in avasada the kulina is only censured,

1527but in aghata the kula suffers harm, and [the kulina] is counted among the kapas.
Through association with kapas many kulinas became disrespected.

1528In this way some time gradually passed,
and Dheyi Bagchi and Madhu Maitra appeared.

1529All the sons of Madhu Maitra by his first wife
became kapas through their father's curse.

1530They ruined the kula of many kulinas,
and Kamsanarayana made manifest the honour of the kapas.

1531When Sri Krishna Chaitanya appeared,
at that time [there was] the power of Raja Kamsanarayana128.

1532Now hear, O hearers, all these events —
how the elevation of the kapas was achieved.

1533A resident of the village of Brahmanbala, Shukadeva Acharya,
the best of brahmanas, lived in Shantipur.

1534In Shantipur he gave a great feast at his father's shraddha;
kulinas and shrotriyas from various places came there.

1535A resident of Shantipur, Narasimha Nadiyal,
came late to that feast129.

1536Brahmanas have a rule: those invited
begin to eat when all have arrived.

1537But that day it turned out otherwise:
all gathered and sat down to eat

1538without waiting for Narasimha Nadiyal.
Arriving, Narasimha Nadli asked the reason.

1539All say: "You do not give your daughters into a great house;
that is why we hold you in contempt.

1540If you can give a daughter to Madhu Maitra,
we shall all together honour you."

1541Narasimha Nadiyal, having suffered humiliation,
quickly went back to his own place.

1542That Nrisimha Pandita, a poor brahmana,
was always thinking of giving his daughter into a great house.

1543"To give a daughter into a great house, money is needed;
how shall I accomplish this?"

1544By providence Raja Sri Ganesha of Srihatta
honoured Narasimha Nadiyal.

1545They had a conversation,
and the king understood what was in Nrisimha's mind.

1546The king says: "Accept the post of minister,
and I shall bear all the expenses of the wedding."

1547Narasimha accepted the post of minister,
and the king gave all that was needed for the wedding130.

1548Having received the money, the noble Narasimha,
together with his wife, sons and two daughters,

1549boarded a boat and went to Majhgram,
where Madhu Maitra lived.

1550Madhu Maitra is performing the morning sandhya and tarpana;
Narasimha went quickly to him.

1551Narasimha says: "Maitra, listen to one thing:
I have fallen into great trouble — be my saviour.

1552Preserve the caste of a brahmana, mahashaya,
otherwise I shall give up my life — I have resolved it."

1553Maitra says: "Mahashaya, if it is within my power,
I shall surely help you."

1554Narasimha says: "Maitra, you are noble;
come with me to where my boat is."

1555Saying this, he took Madhu Maitra into the boat
and brought his two beautiful daughters to him:

1556"Take these two daughters in marriage;
this wealth and these jewels I give as dowry."

1557Maitra says: "Great houses do not take [brides from your family];
I am afraid to take your daughters in marriage."

1558Narasimha says: "If you do not take my daughters,
I shall die with my whole family, and you will be the slayer of a brahmana.

1559With my whole family I shall give up my life in the river —
know for certain, Maitra, this is my vow."

1560When Maitra heard Narasimha's words,
it was as if a thunderbolt had struck his head.

1561"Slaying a brahmana, slaying women — what a terrible plight!"
Seeing this, Madhu Maitra laments greatly:

1562"If I marry, there will be censure in the kulina community;
if I do not, a great sin will fall on me.

1563Compared with [such] a sin, marriage is no fault;
come what may, I shall surely marry."

1564Thinking thus, he reassured Narasimha
and, choosing a day, married both daughters.

1565Seeing this, Madhu Maitra's sons by his former marriage
excluded their father from the community.

1566Madhu Maitra sought refuge with Dheyi Bagchi,
but he at first disregarded him.

1567O hearers, now hear the reason for this disregard:
disclosing it, I shall describe it.

1568Madhu Maitra and Dheyi Bagchi were two great kulinas;
for some reason a long-standing quarrel arose between them.

1569Madhu is the brother-in-law (wife's brother), Dheyi the sister's husband;
at an invitation of Dheyi's Madhu did not eat.

1570Dheyi says: "Listen, Madhu, this is my vow:
I shall make you eat [even] soaked rice."

1571At that time Dheyi had great power:
the kulina community almost entirely obeyed him.

1572Some kulinas were on Madhu Maitra's side,
but they were angered by his marriage to the daughters of Nadli.

1573Madhu's sons, taking all those brahmanas,
went and took Dheyi's side.

1574All the brahmanas abandoned Madhu Maitra;
expelled from the community, Madhu Maitra was left alone.

1575Madhu writes a letter to Dheyi Bagchi:
"In the community I have everywhere become unfit.

1576Preserve my honour, mahashaya;
know for certain that I take refuge in you."

1577The letter bore Madhu no fruit;
then Madhu went to Dheyi's house and ate there.

1578At that time Dheyi Bagchi was elsewhere;
telling his sister, Madhu went home.

1579Gradually some time passed;
the day of Madhu's father's shraddha arrived.

1580Madhu Maitra, to invite Dheyi Bagchi,
came to Dheyi's house.

1581Madhu says: "Bagchi, accept the invitation;
my request is that you act as priest at the shraddha.

1582If you will not accept my words,
I shall not perform the shraddha, and I shall give up my life."

1583At that time Dheyi Bagchi had great power:
the kulina community obeyed him.

1584Then Dheyi Bagchi's wife came and said:
"Conduct his father's shraddha and preserve my brother's honour."

1585Having thought for a long time, Dheyi Bagchi Mahashaya
vowed to protect Madhu Maitra.

1586Dheyi Bagchi, taking the chief kulinas and shrotriyas,
went as an invited guest to the shraddha of Madhu's father.

1587Madhu Maitra's sons, fencing themselves off in the house,
were keeping apart.

1588Dheyi Bagchi, honoured and foremost of all,
summoned Madhu Maitra's sons

1589and asked them to submit to their father;
they did not heed Bagchi's words, and Bagchi grew angry.

1590All the brahmanas present, kulinas and others,
said: "Madhu's sons have become fallen:

1591quarrelling with their father, they have done a wicked deed."
For a deed worthy of kapas they became kapas.

1592Anai, Arjuna and the other sons of the former wife,
becoming disowned sons, were counted among the kapas.

1593They lost their kula through their own misdeeds;
