becoming outcastes, in the end they [nevertheless] rose.

1594Madhu Maitra's sons by his last wife, grandsons of Nadli through their mother,
became the purest in the Maitra family.

1595Raksha, Sadananda, Nanda and the other sons,
grandsons of Nadli through their mother, are chief kulinas.

1596The kapas became outcastes and untouchable;
no kulina or shrotriya associated with them.

1597Then all the kapas conspired
and by various means began to ruin the kula of the kulinas.

1598[When] Dheyi Bagchi and Madhu Maitra had left the world,
the strictures of the community gradually increased.

1599The constraints of the community brought utter ruin:
the kula of kulinas was destroyed in the easiest way.

1600One loses his kula by eating a kapa's food;
another, by bathing at a kapa's ghat, loses his kula;

1601another's kula becomes low from a sprinkling of a kapa's water,
another's kula is diminished by touching a kapa.

1602Good shrotriyas do not want to give daughters to kapas,
and for that reason too the kapas' outrages increase.

1603The zamindar of Tahirpur, Raja Kamsanarayana,
is a shrotriya-nayaka of a shuddha-shrotriya family.

1604Kulinas and genealogists went to him
and began to tell of the ruin of the kula in the easiest way.

1605Kulinas, shrotriyas and genealogists,
taking counsel, determined a remedy.

1606[The rule had been:] if [a kulina] takes a kapa's daughter or gives a daughter to a kapa, the kulina's kula is broken;

1607the karana in the rites of the kula is the chief part for a kulina:
if he makes a karana with a kapa, the kulina's kula is broken.

1608[Now they ruled:] "A shrotriya is a touchstone, like the Ganga:
giving daughters to kapas, they will remain the best.

1609Shrotriyas will give daughters to kapas and kulinas;
kapas will receive seats [in the row] after the kulinas.

1610If one sleeps and eats together with a kapa,
kulinism will never be lost."

1611The raja of Tahirpur, Kamsanarayana,
gave two [of his] daughters to kapas:

1612the first daughter he gave to the son of Vanga Sanyal,
the second daughter he gave to the son of Daora Majhi Sanyal.

1613At these two weddings kapas and kulinas ate together —
thus the elevation of the kapas was achieved.

1614The chief performer [of the rite] is the kulina, the secondary the kapa;
by the raja's efforts the quarrel of kapas and kulinas ended.

1615[A kulina] who takes a kashta-shrotriya's daughter
does not lose kulinism, but becomes subject to censure;

1616by then giving a daughter to a famous kulina
he will again obtain the former honour of the kula.

1617Breaking certain rules of Udayana Bhaduri,
Raja Kamsanarayana established new rules.

1618By these rules all the Varendra brahmanas live;
to this day no one breaks these rules131.

1619I shall tell of the rules in detail in the description of the karana;
know this for certain, O hearers.

1620Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
now I shall recount the names of the melas and patis.

1621The melas of the Radhis and the patis of the Varendras:
by the "faults" the order of the kulas is arranged.

1622I shall describe the thirty-six melas of the Radhis:
Phulia, Vallabhi, Khardaha,

1623Sarvanandi, Surai and Pandita-ratni,
Bangal, Pasmel and Vijaya-panditi,

1624the mela of Gopala Ghataki and Vidyadhari,
Chhaya, Narendri and Acharya-shekhari,

1625the melas of Chandai, Madhai and Parihali,
the mela of Srirangabhatti, Hari Majumdari,

1626the mela of Kakutsthi and Maladhara-khani,
the mela Srivardhini and the mela Pramodini,

1627the mela Shubharaja-khani, Dasharatha Ghataki,
the mela Nadiya, the mela Rai, Bhairava Ghataki,

1628Dohata, the mela Chhayi and Dharadhari,
Chatta-raghavi, Achambita and Bali,

1629the mela Shuddha-sarvanandi, Raghava Ghoshali,
Sadananda-khani and Chandrashekhari;

1630Chandrashekhari's other name is Chandrapati.
The Radhi kulinas are distributed among these thirty-six melas.

1631Now I shall describe the patis of the Varendras:
Nirabil, Bhushana, Rohila,

1632Bhavanipur, Beni and Ale-khani,
the pati Jonali and the pati Kutub-khani.

1633The Varendra kulinas are distributed among eight patis;
O hearers, I have told of the patis132.

1634O hearers, you are most fortunate:
on this occasion I have told of the division of Radhis and Varendras.

1635Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall tell of the parivarta among the Radhis and the karana among the Varendras.

1636Chatuti, Putitunda, Ghoshal, Bandyaghati,
Kanjilal, Ganguli, Kunda[gain] and Mukhuti...

1637In the Kunda family there were many bad deeds,
and Devivara deprived them all of kula:

1638[they] accepted gifts from the unworthy, officiated for those unfit,
married the daughters of kashta-shrotriyas,

1639constantly intermarried with vamshajas —
for all these reasons the Kundas lost their kulinism.

1640In Devi[vara]'s assembly the kulina dignity of the Kundas was lost;
in Devi[vara]'s assembly seven houses kept their kula.

1641Gathering all the faults of the kulinas,
seeing the faults, he carefully determined [their] dignity.

1642By likeness of faults he united [families] into melas, forming equal groups:
by the faults he divided the kulinas into thirty-six melas.

1643As according to sankhya the world arises from prakriti,
so the melas arise from the Mukhutis.

1644Yogeshvara Mukhuti is the original prakriti of the melas:
from him Devivara creates the melas.

1645By Devi[vara]'s skill the whole Mukhuti family
took upon itself the burden of faults and merits:

1646absorbing faults, the Mukhutis became the receptacle of faults and merits —
and Devivara called the Mukhutis "prakriti."

1647Chatuti, Putitunda and Ghoshal,
Bandyaghati, Ganguli and Kanjilal —

1648then they took up the burden of faults and merits
and became the receptacle of faults and merits:

1649through the faults and merits of the Mukhutis they share in faults and merits;
therefore Devivara calls them all "palti."

1650He from whom a fault originates is "prakriti";
he to whom that fault attaches is called "palti."

1651If Rama commits a fault, Rama is the prakriti;
if Shyama is tainted through connection with Rama, Shyama is called palti.

1652Marriages shall be contracted between palti and prakriti —
such was the rule Devivara laid down.

1653The prakritis shall take the daughters of the six palti houses,
and the paltis shall take the daughters of the prakritis.

1654Kulina daughters born of kulina daughters
shall no longer be given in marriage [outside this circle].

1655By this rule the kulina keeps the dignity of his kula;
if one acts otherwise, the [bond of] palti and prakriti is broken.

1656If the [bond of] palti and prakriti is broken, the kula does not remain:
the kulacharyas call such a one a vamshaja.

1657"By only taking or only giving [daughters]
kulinism will not remain," says Devivara.

1658Marriages shall be contracted by the rule of parivarta;
if one acts otherwise, the dignity of the kula will be lost.

1659If, bypassing the prakritis, the paltis alone
intermarry among themselves by parivarta,

1660then the dignity of the kulina's kula will be lost,
and they will be counted among the vamshajas.

1661Kulinas who have no [mutual] exchange [of daughters]
will also be counted among the vamshajas.

1662If a kulina gives a daughter to a vamshaja or a shrotriya,
the kulina will become a vamshaja; [likewise] if he takes a vamshaja's daughter.

1663For up to seven generations a vamshaja retains a little honour,
and after that the vamshaja becomes most contemptible.

1664A vamshaja is like a polluted pot, rejected by kulinas;
many of them, abandoning good deeds, are sunk in bad ones.

1665A good shrotriya does not want to give a daughter to a vamshaja,
but even if he does, the shrotriya's dignity is not lost.

1666A shrotriya can marry the daughters of a kulina,
of a vamshaja and of a shrotriya.

1667A shrotriya is most pure — [like] Ganga water:
he has the power to purify a vamshaja.

1668Many vamshajas, giving daughters to shrotriyas,
by Devi[vara]'s grace easily became shrotriyas.

1669The Banduris of Nadha were vamshajas —
they became shrotriyas of the Mashachataka rank.

1670The Banduris [of the family of] Sundaramalla were vamshajas —
some of them became Batavyal shrotriyas133.

1671Many vamshajas, by giving daughters to shrotriyas,
wish to rise in society by becoming shrotriyas;

1672this caused great turmoil in society,
and Devivara abolished this rule.

1673Accepting gifts from the unworthy and officiating for those unfit
is very common among the vamshajas.

1674Many vamshajas, going to various lands,
perform rites and worship and serve as cooks.

1675Officiating for shudras, serving as temple priests and cooks,
the vamshajas settled in various lands.

1676The kashta-shrotriyas driven out by Devi[vara] and all the vamshajas,
going to various lands, officiate for shudras and others,

1677serve as temple priests and as cooks —
thus the vamshajas came to extreme degradation.

1678Many vamshajas turned to crafts:
they took up the trades of cowherds, potters, jugi weavers and tanti weavers.

1679Of the kashta-shrotriyas and the vamshajas
many became varna-brahmanas.

1680In Ballala's time many became agradanis,
and later many vamshajas joined them.

1681In brahmana society they are objects of censure.
Now, O hearers, hear of the dignity of parivarta.

1682Parivarta means "exchange"; I shall explain it in detail;
fix your minds on it, O hearers.

1683When one takes another's sister and the other takes the first one's daughter,
all call this parivarta.

1684[For example,] Shyama took Rama's sister,
and Rama takes the daughter of [a relative of] Shyama on the other side —

1685this is called the custom of parivarta.
I shall tell in detail how it is done.

1686If the father-in-law or brother-in-law marries the son-in-law's paternal aunt or sister, this is chief (mukhya) parivarta.

1687If the son-in-law has no aunt or sister,
and the father-in-law or brother-in-law takes the daughter of [a relative] on the other side,

1688this too counts as chief parivarta.
Hear, honoured hearers, of secondary (gauna) parivarta:

1689if there is neither aunt nor sister of the son-in-law nor a daughter on the other side, and the father-in-law or brother-in-law marries the daughter of his paternal uncle (younger or elder),

1690— this the kulacharyas call secondary parivarta.

1691If even this is ever impossible,
then that kulina's kula perishes:

1692he is counted among the vamshajas —
know this for certain, O hearers.

1693The son-in-law too may marry his father-in-law's sister, his paternal cousin,
his father-in-law's aunt, his cousin through the elder uncle,

1694the daughter of his brother-in-law's paternal cousin,
and his brother-in-law's daughter —

1695this too counts as parivarta.
Now hear what relationships arise through parivarta:

1696mutually sons-in-law and fathers-in-law, mutually sisters' husbands:
one becomes a father-in-law, another a sister's husband,

1697one a son-in-law, another an aunt's husband —
this is the custom of parivarta among the Radhis.

1698If there is neither aunt nor sister nor daughter,
then for lack of parivarta the kulina's kula perishes.

1699Without parivarta the kula does not remain:
a kulina without parivarta is called a vamshaja.

1700Parivarta takes place between palti and prakriti;
outside palti and prakriti the kula does not remain.

1701Equal standing of kula, equal exchange of gifts (daughters),
equality of both families — this is called "saparyaya."134

1702"Equal standing of kula" means equal kulinism:
equal faults in both kulas, without difference.

1703Mutual exchange of daughters in saparyaya is best;
in the absence of a daughter, the giving and receiving of a girl made of kusha grass.

1704[…]135

1705The exchange of daughters in saparyaya is called the best,
but this rule is very hard to keep.

1706To keep the kula equal one must arrange a "vara" (permission):
the head of the kula (kula-karta) is concerned to give the vara.

1707Those entitled to perform the nandimukha shraddha
are entitled to give daughters in marriage:

1708them the kulacharyas call heads of the kula (kula-karta).
Through the exchange of daughters he gains "merit" (krititva);

1709having gained merit, he obtains the right to give vara:
the honour of a kula-karta who has gained merit is boundless.

1710To keep the pairing equal, the heads of kulas
give vara to a son, a grandson, a brother's son.

1711In this there are three classes: arti, kshemya, uchita;
I shall explain their meaning; hear also of one more, labhya.

1712Vara means "permission"; I shall state its essence:
to the son, grandson or brother's son of the head of the kula

1713the head of the kula says: "You are equal to me;
exchange [daughters] and do not think of anything else."

1714The son, grandson, brother's son, by this vara of the head of the kula,
obtain the right to take and give daughters.

1715Having received the vara, they become equal to the head of the kula:
all faults and merits remain with the head of the kula.

1716The faults and merits [of these marriages] do not [fall] on the sons, grandsons and others: since it is the head of the kula's kula, they remain with the head of the kula.

1717[Those who make] the exchange do not receive its faults and merits —
this property of the vara the kulacharyas make known to all.

1718Thus I have explained the meaning of [the word] "vara";
now, O hearers, hear the meaning of the word "arti."

1719When the head of the kula has given permission,
the son, grandson, brother's son shall give daughters in marriage.

1720If by the vara of the head of the kula one gives in marriage an aunt, sister, daughter, brother's daughter, the kula will be glorified.

1721[As it is said:] "Let the father himself give the daughter, or the brother with the father's permission…" and so on136.

1722If a father's duty is done with his permission,
it is counted as the father's act:

1723being the father's act, it is "in the father's place" (pitri-sthaniya);
even if a son does it, it is not "in the son's place."

1724Such a gift is counted as a gift of the head of the kula:
this is "arti," the "ornament of the head," the honoured "father's place."

1725I have explained the meaning of the word "arti";
O hearers, hear the meaning of the word "kshemya."

1726If, without receiving the permission of the head of the kula,
a son, grandson or brother's son

1727gives in marriage an aunt, sister, daughter, brother's daughter —
this is "kshemya," the "ornament of the feet," the "son's place."

1728If a father's duty is done without his permission,
it will not be "in the father's place":

1729such a gift is counted as the son's act,
therefore it is "in the son's place."

1730Being the "father's place," arti is higher;
being the "son's place," kshemya is lower than arti.

1731I have explained the meaning of the word "kshemya";
O hearers, hear the meaning of the word "uchita."

1732If the head of the kula himself performs his own act,
all call it "uchita," the "equal place."

1733If the head of the kula himself gives in marriage an aunt, sister, daughter, granddaughter, brother's daughter, the kula is glorified.

1734All say this is the best;
after it comes arti, then kshemya.

1735I have explained the meaning of the word "uchita";
O hearers, hear the meaning of the word "labhya."

1736[If] someone, having made an exchange [of daughters], gained merit,
and his younger [brother] has not made an exchange —

1737then by the elder's merit his merit too is acknowledged;
this is what is accepted as "labhya."

1738A son, grandson, brother's son, by the vara of the head of the kula,
gain merit even without having made [an exchange];

1739their younger brothers who did not receive vara,
or who were born after the head of the kula died —

1740for them the receipt of vara is acknowledged through the vara received by the elder;
this is what is accepted as "labhya."

1741[One who] has not gained merit and has not received vara from the head of the kula —
[if] the elder's merit and the vara he received are evident,

1742by them the younger's kulina dignity is established:
this Devivara calls "labhya."

1743I have explained the meaning of the word "labhya";
now I shall tell of the karana among the Varendras.

1744In karana and parivarta the father gives the daughter;
with the father's permission the brothers and others may also [give her].

1745For the increase of the dignity of the kulinas
Udayana created karana and parivarta.

1746Before giving in marriage by parivarta, [they make] a karana —
this became customary among the Varendra kulinas.

1747When daughters or sisters are mutually taken — by oneself or by a son —
it is called parivarta, exchange.

1748Those entitled to perform the nandimukha shraddha
are entitled to give daughters in marriage:

1749they are the heads of the kula, the performers of the karana;
while the grandfather is alive, he is called the performer of the karana.

1750The mutual promise of the performers of the karana to give a daughter or sister
is called the "karana of obligation" (dayer karana).

1751While the grandfather is alive it is the grandfather's act:
therefore at the marriage of a granddaughter or grandson [his karana] is accepted.

1752Honoured hearers, whoever [wishes to know] the detailed meaning of the karana,
I shall show it by an example, and you will be able to understand.

1753The promise concerning the exchange of daughters
the genealogists call the "karana of obligation."

1754The karana concerning the giving of a daughter is called the "karana of obligation":
"obligation" here means the obligation [to give] a daughter — know this for certain.

1755A promise like a betrothal (vagdana),
in which the names of the actual bridegroom and bride are mentioned —

1756the performer of the karana on the bride's side utters it,
and the performer of the karana on the bridegroom's side utters the words of consent.

1757Such is the mutual custom of parivarta;
seeing an example, you will understand the karana for certain.

1758The performer of the karana on the bridegroom's side is Bidhu Maitra,
the performer of the karana on the bride's side is Rama Sanyal.

1759Rama Sanyal utters the promise to give his daughter,
Bidhu Maitra utters the consent to take the daughter.

1760Likewise Bidhu Maitra utters the promise to give his sister,
and Rama Sanyal utters the consent to take that girl.

1761Rama Sanyal promised, according to the rules of karana,
to give his daughter to Bidhu Maitra's son;

1762Bidhu promised, according to the rules of karana,
to marry his son to Rama's daughter;

1763Bidhu Maitra promised, according to the rules of karana,
to give his sister in marriage to Rama Sanyal;

1764Rama promised, according to the rules of karana,
to marry Bidhu's sister.

1765In the presence of kulinas, genealogists and relatives
the mutual promises and consents are uttered thus.

1766Filling an earthen pot with water and putting kusha in it,
they perform the rite according to the rules of betrothal.

1767Gathering with friends, relatives, kulinas and genealogists,
they go to the ghat of a river, canal, lake or pond,

1768and the performers of the karana on both sides, holding that pot,
immerse it in the water — this is called karana.

1769[...] He who by parivarta is the bridegroom's side
is also the bride's side — know for certain137.

1770"The son of so-and-so and the daughter of so-and-so —
the marriage alliance between them is settled" — such is their mutual word.

1771"The karana may be performed on another day
or on the wedding day," says Udayana.

1772First they perform the karana, then the wedding by parivarta —
this rule became established among the kulinas.

1773Raja Kamsanarayana introduced the rule of ekavarta
and created a special "karana of obligation":

1774the performer of the karana on the bride's side performs the karana as before,
in which there will be a promise and a consent;

1775the performer of the karana on the bridegroom's side gives a girl made of kusha,
and the performer of the karana on the bride's side accepts it.

1776On the bride's side the promise to give a daughter, on the bridegroom's side the gift of a kusha girl: such an exchange establishes the "karana of obligation."

1777Seeing an example, O hearers, all will understand;
therefore I shall show one example.

1778The performer of the karana on the bride's side is Shyama Bagchi,
the performer of the karana on the bridegroom's side is Yadu Bhaduri.

1779Shyama promised, according to the rules of karana,
to give his daughter to Yadu Bhaduri's son;

1780Yadu Bhaduri promised, according to the rules of karana,
to marry [his son] to Shyama's daughter.

1781The performer of the karana on the bridegroom's side is Yadu Bhaduri,
the performer of the karana on the bride's side is named Shyama.

1782Yadu will at once give Shyama Bagchi
a kusha daughter or a kusha sister.

1783Accepting the kusha girl, Shyama
will place it in an earthen pot full of water.

1784Gathering with friends, relatives, kulinas and genealogists,
they go to the ghat of a river, canal, lake or pond,

1785and the performer of the karana on the bride's side, holding that pot,
immerses it in the water — this is called karana.

1786The promise to give a real daughter is on the bride's side,
the gift of a kusha girl on the bridegroom's side.

1787Thus the karana is performed through exchange;
this rule the raja established for ekavarta weddings.

1788By day they perform the karana of obligation, at night they give the daughter —
the kulinas proceed by this rule.

1789To preserve the kula of the kulinas
Kamsanarayana established this rule.

1790A kulina who has neither daughter nor sister
preserves his kula by giving a kusha girl.

1791In a parivarta wedding [Udayana's] karana of obligation [applies]:
in the karana of obligation there is an exchange of promises to give daughters.

1792In an ekavarta wedding a promise to give a daughter is made
and a kusha girl is given.

1793The exchange of the promise to give a daughter and the gift of a kusha girl —
this condition Raja Kamsanarayana laid down.

1794Thus two kinds of karana of obligation were established,
and the kulinas hold to the two kinds of karana of obligation.

1795If a kulina takes a daughter without a karana,
his kula will not remain, say the genealogists.

1796At the giving of a daughter they perform the karana of obligation:
without the karana of obligation a kulina does not take a daughter.

1797If, with the bridegroom to whom a daughter is to be given by the karana of obligation, something happens by providence after the karana —

1798if that bridegroom does not marry the girl,
or if the bridegroom dies —

1799that girl is tainted by the fault of "previously given to another" (anyapurva):
no one touches her food and water.

1800Such a girl is never given in marriage;
occasionally a fallen brahmana marries her.

1801Such a girl is called "dhemni":
she is rejected by brahmanas, she has no place in society.

1802If a worthy brahmana marries a dhemni,
he becomes unfit in society and is counted among the fallen.

1803If the karana has been performed, the kula of the father and brother is preserved:
in the karana the father and brother are not guilty for the girl's faults and merits.

1804If after the karana of obligation something happens by providence
and the father or brother do not give the girl to that bridegroom —

1805that girl, as before, becomes fallen,
and her father and brother lose their kulinism:

1806because of the breaking of the kula they go over to the kapas,
but even the kapas do not admit them into the community.

1807For this offence they become most contemptible;
[only] by performing a karana do the kapas rise in society.

1808Thus I have explained the meaning of the karana of obligation;
now, O hearers, hear the meaning of parivarta.

1809If the father-in-law or brother-in-law marries the son-in-law's aunt or sister,
this is called parivarta.

1810Karana and parivarta exist among the kulinas;
later all the kulinas began to perform karana and parivarta.

1811Kaluka (?) Bhatta of the gain Nandanavasi
and Mayura Bhatta of the gain Bhattashali,

1812Mangala Ojha Mahashaya of the gain Karanja —
with the help of these three Udayana performed parivarta and karana.

1813Udayana Acharya and Vallabha Acharya —
these two noble men first performed karana and parivarta:

1814Udayana's daughter was taken by Vallabhacharya,
Vallabha's sister was taken by Udayana's son.

1815The kapas too [perform] karana and parivarta in this way,
but even so the kapas do not become honoured:

1816the kapas are most contemptible in society,
by contact with them the kula of kulinas perishes.

1817Kamsanarayana, giving a daughter to a kapa,
brought them all into society.

1818Making two classes — kulinas the highest, kapas the middle —
by giving a daughter to a kapa he preserves the kapas' dignity.

1819He arranged for kapas and kulinas to eat together:
by a kapa's touch kulinas no longer become kapas.

1820Kamsanarayana made the kapas honourable
and introduced some new rules.

1821"By only taking or only giving [daughters]
the kula will not remain," so says Udayana.

1822Without parivarta and karana the kula does not remain;
for this a daughter or sister is needed.

1823Kulinas who have neither daughter nor sister
lose the dignity of their kula and go over to the kapas.

1824Among the kapas there is only the karana of obligation;
the rules of parivarta and ekavarta do not apply to them.

1825By the karana of obligation [alone] a kapa becomes honoured —
so proclaimed Raja Kamsanarayana.

1826Having performed the karana of obligation, the kapas among themselves
proceed by the rule of parivarta or ekavarta as they wish.

1827Parivarta and ekavarta are between kapa and kapa;
between kapas and kulinas there are no such rules.

1828A kapa who gives a daughter to a kulina is honoured:
such a kapa is a "rich" (adhya) kapa […].

1829A kapa gives a daughter to a kulina after performing a karana of obligation […];
[the raja] introduced ekavarta and the kushamaya-karana.

1830Having performed the karana of obligation, they give a daughter into one house;
having performed the karana of obligation, they take a daughter from another house:

1831giving a daughter into one house and taking a daughter from another house —
this is called the custom of ekavarta.

1832Giving a daughter to a kulina and taking a kulina's daughter —
only this rule applies here.

1833I shall show an example — listen attentively, O hearers:
Rama Sanyal gives his daughter to Shyama Maitra,

1834and Rama Sanyal's son takes Bidhu Lahiri's daughter —
this is called the rule of ekavarta.

1835Having performed the karana of obligation, by ekavarta or by parivarta
all the kulinas exchange [daughters] in this way.

1836Preserving Udayana's karana of obligation and parivarta,
[Kamsanarayana] established one more rule — ekavarta.

1837In ekavarta Maharaja Kamsanarayana
created a karana of obligation of another kind.

1838A kulina who has neither daughter nor sister
does not obtain kulinism for lack of parivarta.

1839Their kula had to be preserved:
otherwise the kula of many kulinas would have perished.

1840Thinking of this, Raja Kamsanarayana
established another rule — the kushamaya-karana.

1841He established kulinism through kusha,
and by this the kula of many kulinas was preserved.

1842[Using] kusha, some [perform] parivarta, others ekavarta:
thus a rule for the giving of daughters was introduced.

1843But in giving a daughter a karana of obligation is required:
without the karana of obligation there is no kulinism.

1844First they perform [the rite with] kusha, then the karana of obligation —
this rule of the raja became customary.

1845If, without performing [the rite with] kusha, one performs the karana of obligation and parivarta, kulinism will still not be obtained.

1846For kulinas who have neither daughter nor sister
the kula is preserved by [the rite with] kusha:

1847if there is neither daughter nor sister, there is no karana of obligation —
their kula is preserved only by the kushamaya-karana.

1848For those who have a daughter or sister
the karana of obligation is prescribed.

1849Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
hear of Raja Kamsanarayana's kushamaya-karana.

1850Performing [the rite with] kusha is called the kushamaya-karana:
"kusha" and "kushamaya-karana" mean the same.

1851Making a bridegroom and a bride of kusha,
they are imagined as a son and a daughter.

1852The exchange [takes place] — a kusha girl for a kusha bridegroom or for a real bridegroom; within one's own gotra — not.

1853If with the words of giving (sampradana) they exchange each side's kusha girl for the other side's kusha bridegroom, the kula will be glorified;

1854if with the words of giving they exchange each side's kusha girl for a real bridegroom, the kula will be glorified.

1855Seeing an example, O hearers, all will understand;
therefore I shall show one example.

1856To Rama's kusha son — Shyama's kusha daughter,
to Shyama's kusha son — Rama's kusha daughter:

1857if such an exchange is made with the words of giving,
this will be the kushamaya-karana.

1858Rama's kusha daughter is given to Shyama,
Shyama's kusha daughter is given to Rama:

1859if this is done, it is called the kushamaya-karana.
Hear what further rules there are in it.

1860An earthen pot full of water is placed in front;
at the end of the words that kusha is put into the pot —

1861the kusha that is imagined as son or daughter
is what they place in the pot.

1862Going to the ghat of a shrotriya's pond,
the two performers of the karana take the pot

1863and immerse it in the water, leaving it there:
know that this is the "kushamaya-karana."

1864In the kulaja-karana [the rite is performed] with kusha;
know that in the upakara-karana too it is with kusha.

1865Kulaja- and upakara-karanas exist among kulinas;
among kapas there are no kulaja- and upakara-karanas.

1866Kulinas perform all the karanas
taking with them kulinas, genealogists and friends.

1867If some kulina, taking a real daughter,
gives her in exchange to another kulina's kusha son —

1868that girl becomes rejected by society:
no one accepts her food and water.

1869Like one "previously given to another," the girl became unfit;
Kamsanarayana abolished this practice.

1870Such a girl is called "kushachharani";
she can no longer live among brahmanas.

1871A kulina who gives his daughter in this way
has no place in society except through the upakara-karana.

1872A kulina's daughter who has neither father nor brother living
is called "nibandhava" ("without kin").

1873The performer of the karana for a daughter or sister is the father or brother;
if there is neither father nor brother, there can be no karana.

1874Without a karana a kulina will not marry her,
and kulina relatives will not give her in marriage.

1875For such a girl the nandimukha shraddha is not performed;
the mother or someone else performs the vriddhi shraddha.

1876Such a girl is given away by the mother or someone else,
and a kapa or a shrotriya takes her.

1877The kulina is high, the kapa lower, the shrotriya lower;
if a kapa or shrotriya marries her, their honour increases.

1878If a kulina marries her, his kula is broken;
if kulina relatives give her away, the kula perishes.

1879A kapa can take a kulina's daughter without a karana:
a kapa takes a nibandhava girl with honour.

1880Shrotriyas have no karana — for them the mark (phonta) is prescribed:
the shrotriya places a mark on the forehead of the bridegroom, kulina or kapa.

1881Placing a mark on the bridegroom's forehead is an honour for the shrotriya:
first the mark is placed, then the daughter is given.

1882When a shrotriya gives a daughter to a shrotriya, a deed (patra) is drawn up —
this rule is current everywhere.

1883Within one's own gotra there is no karana of any kind:
all karanas are performed with another gotra.

1884While the father is alive, kulina brothers
are not entitled to perform a karana:

1885while the father is alive, a kulina's sons
remain within the father's kusha.

1886If any of the brothers meanwhile
performs a karana with a kapa, he becomes a kapa;

1887his father and brothers, tainted, are counted as "pokra":
rejected by kulinas, "suspended kulinas," contemptible.

1888But in the community of kapas they are honoured kulinas:
the kapas respect them, they are honoured in every way.

1889After the father's death the kulina brothers
must carefully divide the kusha.

1890The kushamaya-karana is called "kusha" —
believe this, O hearers.

1891With kulinas they perform [the kusha] each separately —
thus the division of their kusha takes place.

1892If the kulina brothers do not perform [the rite with] kusha,
they are not counted among the kulinas.

1893For this reason the kulina brothers
perform the kushamaya-karana each separately:

1894one's kusha does not give kulinism to another —
therefore each performs a separate kusha.

1895The kusha that kulina brothers perform after the father's death
is called the "kulaja-karana."

1896The kulaja-karana attests kulinism;
in other karanas too one must perform the kusha.

1897If the kulaja-karana is performed at the ghat of a siddha-shrotriya,
the shrotriya thereby obtains the rank of nayaka.

1898If after the father's death one of the kulina brothers,
without dividing the kusha, performs a karana with a kapa,

1899then all his other brothers
become tainted and are counted as "bhai-kara."

1900If a kulina himself performs a karana with a kapa,
he together with his sons is counted among the kapas.

1901If sons with the kulina's permission
perform a karana with a kapa,

1902they together with their father become kapas.
But if a son, without the permission of his kulina father,

1903of his own will performs a karana with a kapa,
he becomes a kapa and remains in the community of kapas.

1904If the father accepts such a son,
[he] is expelled from the kulina community;

1905but if the father rejects that son, […]138

1906yet the fault of "avadhyata" (disobedience) falls on them.
I shall tell how the faults of "pokra," "bhai-kara" and "avadhyata" are expiated:

1907for the expiation of all these offences
one performs a kushamaya-karana with an equal house.

1908By the kushamaya-karana all these faults are removed —
all call it the "upakara-karana" (karana of benefit).

1909If a kulina's kula is tainted by a fault,
he performs a kushamaya-karana with an equal house:

1910the fault goes, and the kulina obtains benefit (upakara) —
that is why it is called the "upakara-karana."

1911Although the rule that a kulina
takes a shrotriya's daughter does exist —

1912taking a shrotriya's daughter is not very praiseworthy for a kulina:
having taken a shrotriya's daughter, one must perform an upakara-karana.

1913If the kulina who has taken a shrotriya's daughter
has his father living,

1914his father performs the upakara-karana;
if there is no father, he must perform it himself.

1915If he himself dies without performing the karana,
his son must perform the upakara-karana.

1916Between two kulinas who have taken shrotriyas' daughters
no upakara-karana is performed;

1917but if they [both] have also taken kulinas' daughters,
then they may perform an upakara-karana.

1918If two kulinas who have taken shrotriyas' daughters perform [between themselves] an upakara-karana, the fault of "pani-niya" (?) arises;

1919by performing three upakara-karanas this fault goes.
And on taking a shrotriya's daughter one must perform one, two or three karanas:

1920one who takes a great shrotriya's daughter — one karana,
one who takes a middle shrotriya's daughter — two karanas,

1921one who takes a small shrotriya's daughter — three karanas:
having performed them, the kulinas become free [of fault].

1922If a kulina, not performing upakara-karanas,
gradually takes six shrotriyas' daughters,

1923the fault of "six shrotriyas" arises in his kula:
the kula does not perish, but [he] is counted lower.

1924All [kinds of] karana exist among kulinas;
among kapas only the karana of obligation remains.

1925Having performed the karana of obligation, [a kapa] will give a daughter to a kulina; having performed the karana of obligation, he will take a kulina's daughter:

1926by this the kapa's dignity increases,
and the kulinas thereby become kapas.

1927A kapa may take a nibandhava girl without a karana;
even taking her without a karana, the kapa will be glorified.

1928A kapa may take a kulina's daughter without a karana;
even if he takes her without a karana, the kapa's honour greatly increases.

1929Without a karana a kapa does not take a kapa's daughter:
in giving daughters between kapas a karana of obligation must be performed.

1930If a kulina without a karana takes a daughter from a kapa,
the kulina's kula is broken, he is counted among the kapas;

1931if a kulina, having performed a karana, takes a daughter from a kapa,
the kulina's kula is broken, he is counted among the kapas.

1932By any other contact with kapas the kula is not lost —
this rule Raja Kamsanarayana Raya established.

1933In Udayana's karana of obligation there is kusha-water,
but no kusha girl is present in it;

1934in the raja's karana of obligation there is a kusha girl —
this difference I have already described.

1935In all the other karanas there is a kusha girl,
and in some there is also a kusha son.

1936No other kusha exists in the community of kapas:
among kapas the kusha is only the kusha of obligation, so I find.

1937If a kapa wishes, he may divide the kusha
even while his father is alive — so it is prescribed:

1938if a kapa's son performs a karana of obligation,
then his kusha becomes separate.

1939The fathers of kapas [whose sons] have divided the kusha
are no longer entitled to a karana;

1940if afterwards children are born to them,
they bear the fault of "garbha-shuda."

1941The earlier sons have no fault,
but the later sons are ruined by the fault of "garbha-shuda":

1942a "garbha-shuda" has no right to a karana,
while the earlier sons have the right to a karana.

1943If a kulina's son or another relative
or people unrelated to the kulina,

1944against the kulina's will or without his knowledge,
give [the kulina's] daughter to a kapa or a shrotriya —

1945then, if they gave her to a kapa, the kulina becomes a kapa, and if to a shrotriya,
the kulina becomes a shrotriya — so say the kulacharyas.

1946If a kapa gives his daughter to a shrotriya,
the kapa becomes a shrotriya — so it is prescribed.

1947If a kapa's son or another relative
or people unrelated to the kapa,

1948against the kapa's will or without his knowledge,
give his daughter to a shrotriya —

1949the kapa will still become a shrotriya:
know for certain, there is no expiation for it.

1950Such a kulina or kapa is called "shrotriyanta":
no expiation is provided for him.

1951This happened after Kamsanarayana,
and no one has since established an expiation.

1952The shrotriya is most pure, like the Ganga:
he gives daughters to kapas and kulinas.

1953If he gives a daughter to a kulina — honour to the shrotriya,
and if he gives a daughter to a kapa, the honour does not change.

1954If kapas, having become shrotriyas, give a daughter to a kulina,
the kulina's kulinism does not waver at all.

1955If a kulina gives a daughter to a shrotriya,
the kulina will become a shrotriya — so it is prescribed;

1956if a kulina, having become a shrotriya, gives a daughter to a kulina,
the kulinism of the kulina who takes the daughter does not waver.

1957If a kulina gives a daughter without a karana
or takes [a daughter] without a karana,

1958the kulina will become a shrotriya — this rule was introduced;
this rule binds kulinas with kulinas.

1959But between kapas and kulinas there is no such rule:
if a kapa gives a daughter without a karana

1960or takes [a daughter] without a karana,
the kapa will become a shrotriya — such is the rule.

1961This rule was introduced between kapa and kapa;
this rule Raja Kamsanarayana established139.

1962With whomever the kushamaya-karana has been performed,
with him there is no karana of obligation;

1963without the karana of obligation there is no exchange [of daughters],
and for an exchange the kusha must be broken.

1964For example, Sadhu Maitra and Bidhu Lahiri have performed a kushamaya-karana —
these two will not exchange daughters.

1965If these two need to exchange [daughters],
they break that kusha and perform kusha with others:

1966Sadhu Maitra performs a kushamaya-karana with Rama Sanyal,
Bidhu Lahiri establishes kusha with Shyama Bhaduri;

1967thus the kusha of Sadhu Maitra and Bidhu Lahiri is broken,
and between these two the exchange proceeds.

1968By this example, honoured hearers,
you will understand [the order] of all the gotras.

1969If shrotriyas ever wish
to pass from a lower pati to a higher one,

1970they must give a daughter to a kapa:
leaving the fault with the kapa, they will pass to the higher pati.

1971Formerly good shrotriyas did not give daughters to kapas,
and the kapas felt this as a humiliation to themselves.

1972The shuddha-shrotriya Raja Kamsanarayana
gave two daughters among the kapas —

1973from that the quarrel of kapas and kulinas ended:
the raja had kapas and kulinas eat together.

1974Through the shrotriyas the kapas obtained deliverance:
by obtaining shrotriyas' daughters the kapas raise their name.

1975Taking a shrotriya's daughter is an honour for a kapa:
the kapas eagerly take shrotriyas' daughters.

1976Kamsanarayana delivered the kapas,
introducing all these new rules.

1977Establishing kulinism through kusha,
he preserved the kula of many kulinas:

1978those who had neither daughter nor sister
kept their kula through the gift of a kusha girl.

1979Through kusha alone he preserved
the boundless kulina dignity of all the kulinas.

1980By these rules all the kulinas live;
the protector of kapas and kulinas is Kamsanarayana.

1981About two hundred years before Gauranga's birth
the power of Udayana Bhaduri arose140.

1982The harm that Udayana did by creating the kapas
was all repaired by Kamsanarayana.

1983The parivarta of the Radhis and Varendras differs;
O hearers, I shall tell something of the difference.

1984The sister of the head of the kula, the daughter of his elder or younger uncle,
his aunt, granddaughter, brother's daughter and daughter —

1985through them the parivarta of the Radhis takes place.
I shall tell, honoured ones, of the parivarta of the Varendras:

1986the sister of the performer of the karana and his real daughter,
and in the kushamaya-karana a kusha daughter:

1987through all these the parivarta of the Varendras takes place;
know this for certain, O hearers.

1988In the Radhi kula is Nityananda, the jewel of virtues;
among the Varendras are counted Advaita and Gadadhara.

1989In the two kulas two Prabhus appeared141 —
[therefore] the Thakurani ordered the kulas of the Radhis and Varendras to be described.

1990Holding in my heart my guru's mighty order,
I have briefly described the kulas of the Radhis and Varendras142.

1991In the year Shaka fourteen hundred and ninety-five
Vrindavana Dasa composed the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata143.

1992Krishnadasa Kaviraja, living in Vrindavana,
in the year Shaka fifteen hundred and three,

1993on a Sunday, on the fifth day of the dark half of Jyaishtha,
completed the book Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita.

1994As it is said in the Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita: "In the Shaka [year] 'fire (3), zero (0), arrows (5), moon (1),' in [the month of] Jyaishtha, in Vrindavana, on a Sunday, on the fifth day of the dark half, this book was completed."144

1995Having completed the book, Krishnadasa Kaviraja,
the king of devotees, wrote this verse.

1996When the year Shaka fifteen hundred and twenty-two came
and the month of Phalguna arrived,

1997on the thirteenth day of the dark half, with joy in my heart,
I completed the book Sri Prema-vilasa145.

1998From the first to the eighteenth vilasa I wrote while living in Khanda,
the two vilasas, nineteenth and twentieth, I wrote after going to Khardaha,

1999and the four vilasas — twenty-first, twenty-second, twenty-third and twenty-fourth —
I wrote joyfully while living in Katwa146.

2000In the "Half-vilasa" I set out the index of the book
and placed the letters of Sri Jiva Gosani, Srinivasa and Narottama:

2001the letters were obtained when the book was finished —
therefore I placed them in the "Half-vilasa."

2002Having completed the book in old age,
I offered it at the root of Virachandra's feet.

2003Writing in old age, one constantly errs:
whatever came to mind at whatever time, that I wrote down.

2004Earlier things I wrote later, and later things earlier:
reflecting, I wrote the book [recording] whatever came to mind.

2005One and the same thing I have written many times:
not all events were always in my memory.

2006Having begun to write about someone,
I wrote in one chapter as much as came to mind;

2007some days later another event of his life
came into my mind and was added,

2008and I described it in another chapter —
that is why I have the fault of repetition.

2009Having composed the book, I could not correct it —
that is why many faults remain in the book.

2010I am old, my body is stricken with illness —
that is why I could not correct the book.

2011O hearers, you are all most fortunate:
mercifully forgive me this fault.

2012Bowing down, I make this request:
correcting the errors, preserve this book.

2013Some events I wrote down having seen them myself,
others I wrote hearing of them from others —

2014and for that reason too the fault of repetition arose:
not everything came to mind at one time.

2015This book I have written obeying my guru's order;
whether I have written well or badly I do not know.

2016O devotees of Krishna, all of you noble:
mercifully place your feet upon my head.

2017Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda, Sri Advaita Raya,
Gadadhara, Srivasa and all the devotees,

2018mercifully place your feet upon my head,
that my offences may go and the bonds of worldly existence be loosed.

2019Srinivasa, Narottama, Prabhu Shyamananda,
mercifully cut my worldly bonds.

2020O guru, ocean of compassion, purifier of the fallen,
you gave me your sight in the form of Sri Jahnava.

2021Prabhu Virachandra showed me love;
mercifully place the feet of both upon my head.

2022That at the last hour I may attain my guru's feet —
this is the desire of my heart which I make known to you.

2023He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.
